candidates.heading: 7.A Server Positioning — Outside Court
candidates.content:
7.A.2 Outside Court. Neither of the server’s feet is allowed to be in
contact with the court when the serve is hit.

candidates.heading: 25.A Wheelchair Play — Serving
candidates.content:
25.A.8 Serving. The moment the ball is served, both large rear wheels
must be on the playing surface behind the baseline and must not
touch anywhere outside the correct serving area. The front
(smaller) wheels are allowed to extend into the court when the
serve is hit.

candidates.heading: 20.E.2 Replays — Replay – Questionable Foot Contact Outside the
candidates.content:
20.E.2.e Replay – Questionable Foot Contact Outside the
Serving Area. When it is questionable whether either
of the server’s feet were in contact with the playing
surface outside the serving area when the paddle
contacted the ball, the referee may call for a replay.

candidates.heading: 25.A Wheelchair Play — Propelling Wheelchair with Foot
candidates.content:
25.A.7 Propelling Wheelchair with Foot. A player who is unable to
propel their wheelchair with one or both upper extremities
(arms) for the entire duration of a match is permitted to propel
the wheelchair using a single foot against the ground. The player
is then subject to the following restrictions for the entire
duration of the match:
1) The player must not utilize their upper extremities for
propulsion.
2) The player’s foot must not be in contact with the ground
when the player strikes the ball to make a shot.
3) The player’s lower extremities must not contact any
wheelchair wheel.

candidates.heading: 20.E.2 Replays — Replay – Questionable Foot Contact with Serving
candidates.content:
20.E.2.d Replay – Questionable Foot Contact with Serving
Area. When it is questionable whether either of the
server’s feet were in contact with the serving area
when the paddle contacted the ball, the referee may
call for a replay.

candidates.heading: Serve Placement
candidates.content:
7.E Serve Placement. The server must serve to the service court diagonally
opposite their correct position. (See Rule 14.B.3 for mini-singles.) The served
ball must clear the opponent’s non-volley zone, with or without touching the
net, and land in the correct service court.

candidates.heading: 5.B Doubles — Player Positions During Rallies
candidates.content:
5.B.4 Player Positions During Rallies. Except while serving and
receiving, there is no restriction on the position of the players, on
or off the court, as long as they are on their respective end of the
net while the ball is live, except when a player crosses the plane of
the net as allowed in Rule 13.I.

candidates.heading: 25.A.7 Propelling Wheelchair with Foot — Fault – Prohibited Actions
candidates.content:
25.A.7.a Fault – Prohibited Actions. For a wheelchair player
who is allowed to use a single foot against the
ground for propulsion, when any upper extremity
contacts a wheelchair wheel, their foot is in contact
with the ground when they hit the ball, or any lower
extremity contacts any wheelchair wheel, it is a fault
against the player.

candidates.heading: 13.I Player Crossing Plane of Net — Ball Crosses Back to Opponent’s Side
candidates.content:
13.I.2 Ball Crosses Back to Opponent’s Side. When a ball bounces in the
court on the receiving player’s end of the net and then returns to
the opponent’s side of the net without being hit, the receiving
player may cross over, under, or around the net to hit the ball, but
only after the ball has first crossed back to the opponent’s end of
the net.

candidates.content:
7.A.2.a Fault – Server Contacting Court. If a server’s foot is in
contact with the court when the serve is hit, it is a fault
against the server.

candidates.content:
7.D.4 Bounce Location. Before the server hits the ball to make the serve,
there is no restriction on where the ball bounces on the playing
surface.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 6: Player Readiness and Calling the
candidates.heading: 6.C When to Serve — Fault – Early Serve
candidates.content:
6.C.1 Fault – Early Serve. When the server hits the serve while the score
is being called, it is a fault against the server.
6.D 10-Second Rule. The server must serve the ball within 10 seconds after the
score call is completed.

candidates.heading: 3.A.4 Lines and Areas — Serving Areas
candidates.content:
3.A.4.g Serving Areas. The areas behind the baseline on each
end of the court. The right and left serving areas are
bounded by and include the imaginary extensions of
their adjacent sideline and the centerline.

candidates.heading: 7.E Serve Placement — Fault – Serve Lands Out of Bounds
candidates.content:
7.E.1 Fault – Serve Lands Out of Bounds. When a served ball lands
outside the correct service court, it is a fault against the server.

candidates.heading: 19.C Matches with Line Judges — Player Responsibilities
candidates.content:
19.C.2 Player Responsibilities. Players are responsible for making
“out” calls for only the service court centerline on their end of
the court.

candidates.heading: Matches Without Line Judges
candidates.content:
19.B Matches Without Line Judges. In matches officiated by a referee without
line judges, players are responsible for making “out” calls for the baseline,
sidelines, and center service line on their end of the court.

candidates.heading: 20.E.2 Replays — Replay – Volley Serve, Questionable Paddle Head
candidates.content:
20.E.2.g Replay – Volley Serve, Questionable Paddle Head
Height. When it is questionable whether the highest
point of the paddle head was no higher than the
server’s wrist joint when the paddle contacted the
ball to make a volley serve, the referee may call for a
replay.

candidates.heading: 14.B Mini-Singles — Shot Placement
candidates.content:
14.B.3 Shot Placement. Each player’s served and returned balls must
land in bounds of the opponent’s side of the court that is in play.

candidates.heading: 20.E.1 Faults — Fault – Volley Serve, Paddle Head Above Wrist.
candidates.content:
20.E.1.b Fault – Volley Serve, Paddle Head Above Wrist.
When the highest point of the paddle head is clearly
above the server’s wrist joint when the paddle
contacts the ball, it is a fault against the server.

candidates.heading: 7.C Volley Serve — Ball Height
candidates.content:
7.C.3 Ball Height. The ball must clearly be no higher than the server’s
waist when the paddle contacts the ball.

candidates.heading: 3.A.4 Lines and Areas — Service Courts
candidates.content:
3.A.4.f Service Courts. The areas on each end of the court
between the non-volley zone and the baseline on
either side of the centerline. The right and left service
courts are bounded by and include their adjacent
baseline, sideline, and the centerline.

candidates.heading: 7.C Volley Serve — Fault – Illegal Volley Serve
candidates.content:
7.C.5 Fault – Illegal Volley Serve. When the server violates Rule 7.C.1,
7.C.2, or 7.C.3, it is a fault against the server.

candidates.heading: 5.A Singles — Holding Serve
candidates.content:
5.A.2 Holding Serve. A player continues to serve, alternating right and
left serving areas after each point won, until the player loses a rally.

candidates.heading: 7.D Drop Serve — Forehand or Backhand
candidates.content:
7.D.5 Forehand or Backhand. The serve can be made with a forehand or
backhand motion.

candidates.heading: 20.E.2 Replays — Replay – Volley Serve, Questionable Upward
candidates.content:
20.E.2.f Replay – Volley Serve, Questionable Upward
Service Motion. When it is questionable whether the
server’s arm was moving in an upward arc when the
paddle contacted the ball to make a volley serve, the
referee may call for a replay.

candidates.heading: 7.D Drop Serve — Number of Bounces
candidates.content:
7.D.3 Number of Bounces. Before the server hits the ball to make the
serve, there is no restriction on how many times the ball can
bounce.

candidates.heading: 7.C Volley Serve — Forehand or Backhand
candidates.content:
7.C.4 Forehand or Backhand. The serve can be made with a forehand or
backhand motion.

candidates.heading: Volley Serve
candidates.content:
7.C Volley Serve. The service motion for a volley serve must comply with Rules
7.C.1 through 7.C.4.

suppliedEvidence.heading: 7.A Server Positioning — Outside Court
suppliedEvidence.content:
7.A.2 Outside Court. Neither of the server’s feet is allowed to be in
contact with the court when the serve is hit.

suppliedEvidence.heading: 25.A Wheelchair Play — Serving
suppliedEvidence.content:
25.A.8 Serving. The moment the ball is served, both large rear wheels
must be on the playing surface behind the baseline and must not
touch anywhere outside the correct serving area. The front
(smaller) wheels are allowed to extend into the court when the
serve is hit.

suppliedEvidence.heading: 20.E.2 Replays — Replay – Questionable Foot Contact Outside the
suppliedEvidence.content:
20.E.2.e Replay – Questionable Foot Contact Outside the
Serving Area. When it is questionable whether either
of the server’s feet were in contact with the playing
surface outside the serving area when the paddle
contacted the ball, the referee may call for a replay.

suppliedEvidence.heading: 25.A Wheelchair Play — Propelling Wheelchair with Foot
suppliedEvidence.content:
25.A.7 Propelling Wheelchair with Foot. A player who is unable to
propel their wheelchair with one or both upper extremities
(arms) for the entire duration of a match is permitted to propel
the wheelchair using a single foot against the ground. The player
is then subject to the following restrictions for the entire
duration of the match:
1) The player must not utilize their upper extremities for
propulsion.
2) The player’s foot must not be in contact with the ground
when the player strikes the ball to make a shot.
3) The player’s lower extremities must not contact any
wheelchair wheel.

suppliedEvidence.heading: 20.E.2 Replays — Replay – Questionable Foot Contact with Serving
suppliedEvidence.content:
20.E.2.d Replay – Questionable Foot Contact with Serving
Area. When it is questionable whether either of the
server’s feet were in contact with the serving area
when the paddle contacted the ball, the referee may
call for a replay.

suppliedEvidence.heading: Serve Placement
suppliedEvidence.content:
7.E Serve Placement. The server must serve to the service court diagonally
opposite their correct position. (See Rule 14.B.3 for mini-singles.) The served
ball must clear the opponent’s non-volley zone, with or without touching the
net, and land in the correct service court.

suppliedEvidence.heading: 5.B Doubles — Player Positions During Rallies
suppliedEvidence.content:
5.B.4 Player Positions During Rallies. Except while serving and
receiving, there is no restriction on the position of the players, on
or off the court, as long as they are on their respective end of the
net while the ball is live, except when a player crosses the plane of
the net as allowed in Rule 13.I.

suppliedEvidence.heading: 25.A.7 Propelling Wheelchair with Foot — Fault – Prohibited Actions
suppliedEvidence.content:
25.A.7.a Fault – Prohibited Actions. For a wheelchair player
who is allowed to use a single foot against the
ground for propulsion, when any upper extremity
contacts a wheelchair wheel, their foot is in contact
with the ground when they hit the ball, or any lower
extremity contacts any wheelchair wheel, it is a fault
against the player.

authorityReviewCandidates.heading: 13.I Player Crossing Plane of Net — Ball Crosses Back to Opponent’s Side
authorityReviewCandidates.content:
13.I.2 Ball Crosses Back to Opponent’s Side. When a ball bounces in the
court on the receiving player’s end of the net and then returns to
the opponent’s side of the net without being hit, the receiving
player may cross over, under, or around the net to hit the ball, but
only after the ball has first crossed back to the opponent’s end of
the net.

authorityReviewCandidates.heading: 7.A.2 Outside Court — Fault – Server Contacting Court
authorityReviewCandidates.content:
7.A.2.a Fault – Server Contacting Court. If a server’s foot is in
contact with the court when the serve is hit, it is a fault
against the server.

authorityReviewCandidates.heading: 9.B Faults — Calling Non-Volley Zone Faults and Service Foot Faults on
authorityReviewCandidates.content:
9.B.3 Calling Non-Volley Zone Faults and Service Foot Faults on
Opponent. Players may only call non-volley zone faults and service
foot faults on an opponent.

higher than the server’s waist when the paddle
contacted the ball to make a volley serve, the referee
may call for a replay.

candidates.heading: Definitions
candidates.content:
Section 2 Definitions
Ball In Play. The timeframe during which a rally is played, from when the serve is
hit until the ball becomes dead.
Carry. Hitting the ball in such a way that it does not bounce away from the paddle
but is carried along on the face of the paddle.
Coaching. Communication of information (including verbal, nonverbal, and
electronic) from someone other than a player’s partner, that players may act upon
to gain an advantage or help them avoid a rules violation.
Court. The area inside the outer dimensions of the baselines and sidelines.
Dead Ball. A ball that is no longer in play.
Distraction. Physical actions by a player that are not common to the game and
interfere with the opponent’s ability or concentration to hit the ball. Examples
include, but are not limited to, making loud noises, stomping feet, and
waving the paddle in an erratic manner.
Double Bounce. When the ball bounces twice on one end of the net before it is
returned.
Double Hit. Hitting the ball twice before it is returned.
Drop Serve. A serve made by dropping the ball and hitting the ball with the paddle
after the ball bounces on the playing surface.
Ejection. Removal of a player from tournament competition for a flagrant or
injurious behavioral violation.
Expulsion. Banishment of a player from the tournament venue for a flagrant or
injurious behavioral violation.
Fault. A rules violation that results in a dead ball and the loss of a rally.
First Server (Doubles). The player who begins the team’s service rotation from
the right serving area after a side out.
Forfeit. The awarding of a game or a match to the opponent due to a violation of
the rules.
Hinder. Any transient element or occurrence not caused by a player that adversely
impacts play. Examples include, but are not limited to, stray balls, flying insects,

candidates.heading: 7.A.2 Outside Court — Fault – Server Contacting Court
candidates.content:
7.A.2.a Fault – Server Contacting Court. If a server’s foot is in
contact with the court when the serve is hit, it is a fault
against the server.

candidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
candidates.heading: TEAM/GAME RULES
candidates.content:
5.9. Spectator Interference: Spectators/non-participants must not be consulted on any call,
nor shall they influence any calls or decisions on the court.
5.10. Video Recording: Video recording is allowed only if all players give their approval before
the game starts.
5.11. Rescheduling & Score Submission Deadlines: If both coaches agree, games may be
rescheduled to a diƯerent time on the same day or to another day within the same week.
However, all game scores must be submitted by the end of Sunday of the same week by
midnight. If this deadline cannot be met due to weather conditions or other unforeseen
circumstances, the Home Captain must notify info@lwrpickleballclub.com before
Sunday at midnight with the rescheduled date and time. Failure to do so may result in
forfeiture of the games.
5.12. Makeup Game Deadline: All makeup games must be played at least one week before the
playoƯs/championship date.
5.13. Weather Interruptions & Mid-Match Stoppages: If weather or other factors interrupt
play after a match has started, the following rules apply based on progress:
5.13.1. Less than half of the games completed: Remaining games should be
rescheduled. Only fully completed games will count toward final scores;
unfinished or unplayed games will not be recorded.
5.13.2. At least half of the games are completed: Completed results will stand. Any
remaining unplayed games may be either rescheduled or canceled as agreed upon
by both Captains (rescheduling is the preferred option).

candidates.heading: 7.A.3 In Serving Area — Fault – Server Outside Serving Area
candidates.content:
7.A.3.a Fault – Server Outside Serving Area. If a server’s foot is
in contact with the playing surface outside the correct
serving area when the serve is hit, it is a fault against the
server.

candidates.heading: 7.A.1 Grounded — Fault – Server Not Grounded
candidates.content:
7.A.1.a Fault – Server Not Grounded. When both server’s feet
are off the playing surface when the serve is hit, it is a
fault against the server.

candidates.heading: 7.E Serve Placement — Fault – Serve Hits Server or Server’s Partner
candidates.content:
7.E.4 Fault – Serve Hits Server or Server’s Partner. When a served ball
contacts the server or server’s partner or anything that is worn or
carried by either, it is a fault against the server.

candidates.heading: 25.B.2 Assistive Devices — Fault – Outside Serving Area
candidates.content:
25.B.2.f Fault – Outside Serving Area. If a server’s assistive
device is in contact with the playing surface outside
the correct serving area when the serve is hit, it is a
fault against the server. (Modifies Rule 7.A.3.a)

candidates.heading: 7.E Serve Placement — Fault – Serve Hits Permanent Object
candidates.content:
7.E.3 Fault – Serve Hits Permanent Object. When a served ball
contacts a permanent object before landing, it is a fault against the
server.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 6: Player Readiness and Calling the
candidates.heading: 6.C When to Serve — Fault – Early Serve
candidates.content:
6.C.1 Fault – Early Serve. When the server hits the serve while the score
is being called, it is a fault against the server.
6.D 10-Second Rule. The server must serve the ball within 10 seconds after the
score call is completed.

candidates.heading: 7.C Volley Serve — Fault – Illegal Volley Serve
candidates.content:
7.C.5 Fault – Illegal Volley Serve. When the server violates Rule 7.C.1,
7.C.2, or 7.C.3, it is a fault against the server.

candidates.heading: 7.E Serve Placement — Fault – Serve Hits Receiver or Receiver’s Partner
candidates.content:
7.E.5 Fault – Serve Hits Receiver or Receiver’s Partner. When a served
ball contacts the receiver or receiver’s partner or anything that is
worn or carried by either, before landing, it is a fault against the
receiver.

candidates.heading: 20.E.1 Faults — Fault – Volley Serve, No Upward Service Motion.
candidates.content:
20.E.1.a Fault – Volley Serve, No Upward Service Motion.
When the server’s arm is not clearly moving in an
upward arc when the paddle contacts the ball, it is a
fault against the server.

candidates.heading: 25.A.8 Serving — Fault – Wheel Outside Serving Area
candidates.content:
25.A.8.c Fault – Wheel Outside Serving Area. If a large rear
wheel of a server’s wheelchair is in contact with the
playing surface outside the correct serving area
when the serve is hit, it is a fault against the server.
(Modifies Rule 7.A.3.a)

candidates.heading: 25.A.8 Serving — Fault – Wheel Not Grounded
candidates.content:
25.A.8.a Fault – Wheel Not Grounded. If either or both large
rear wheels of a server’s wheelchair are off the
playing surface when the serve is hit, it is a fault
against the server. (Modifies Rule 7.A.1.a)

candidates.heading: 10.A Two-Bounce Rule — Fault – No Bounce by Serving Side
candidates.content:
10.A.2 Fault – No Bounce by Serving Side. When the server or server’s
partner does not allow the return of serve to bounce before hitting
the ball, it is a fault against the serving side.

candidates.heading: 20.E.1 Faults — Fault – Drop Serve, Force Added to Ball Release.
candidates.content:
20.E.1.f Fault – Drop Serve, Force Added to Ball Release.
When the server propels the ball in any direction or
manner prior to hitting the ball to make a drop serve,
it is a fault against the server.

candidates.heading: 20.E.1 Faults — Fault – Volley Serve, Ball Contacted Above Waist.
candidates.content:
20.E.1.c Fault – Volley Serve, Ball Contacted Above Waist.
When the ball is clearly above the server’s waist
when the paddle contacts the ball, it is a fault against
the server.

candidates.heading: 7.E Serve Placement — Fault – Serve Lands Out of Bounds
candidates.content:
7.E.1 Fault – Serve Lands Out of Bounds. When a served ball lands
outside the correct service court, it is a fault against the server.

candidates.heading: 7.E Serve Placement — Fault – Serve Lands in Non-Volley Zone
candidates.content:
7.E.2 Fault – Serve Lands in Non-Volley Zone. When a served ball lands
in the non-volley zone, it is a fault against the server.

candidates.heading: 25.A.8 Serving — Fault – Wheel Contacting Court
candidates.content:
25.A.8.b Fault – Wheel Contacting Court. If a large rear
wheel of a server’s wheelchair is in contact with the
court when the serve is hit, it is a fault against the
server. (Modifies Rule 7.A.2.a)

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 6: Player Readiness and Calling the
candidates.heading: Fault – 10-Second Violation
candidates.content:
6.D.1 Fault – 10-Second Violation. When the server does not serve
within 10 seconds after the score is called, it is a fault against the
server.

candidates.heading: 10.C Returned Ball Placement — Fault – Ball Hits Player
candidates.content:
10.C.3 Fault – Ball Hits Player. After the serve, when the ball contacts a
player or anything that is worn or carried by the player, except the
player’s paddle or the player’s hands below the wrist joint while in
contact with the paddle, it is a fault against that player.

candidates.heading: 20.E.1 Faults — Fault – Volley Serve and Drop Serve, Spin or
candidates.content:
20.E.1.e Fault – Volley Serve and Drop Serve, Spin or
Manipulation on Release. When the server
manipulates or spins the ball immediately prior to
the serve, it is a fault against the server.

candidates.heading: 7.D Drop Serve — Fault – Illegal Drop Serve
candidates.content:
7.D.6 Fault – Illegal Drop Serve. When the server violates Rule 7.D.1 or
7.D.2, it is a fault against the server.

candidates.heading: 20.E.1 Faults — Fault – Drop Serve, Ball Release Aided Height.
candidates.content:
20.E.1.g Fault – Drop Serve, Ball Release Aided Height.
When the server does not clearly release the ball
from a natural (un-aided) height, it is a fault against
the server.

candidates.heading: 20.E.1 Faults — Fault – Volley Serve, Paddle Head Above Wrist.
candidates.content:
20.E.1.b Fault – Volley Serve, Paddle Head Above Wrist.
When the highest point of the paddle head is clearly
above the server’s wrist joint when the paddle
contacts the ball, it is a fault against the server.

candidates.heading: 20.E.1 Faults — Fault – Volley Serve and Drop Serve, Release from
candidates.content:
20.E.1.d Fault – Volley Serve and Drop Serve, Release from
Hands and Paddle. When the server does not clearly
release the ball from only one hand or only from the
paddle immediately prior to the serve, it is a fault
against the server.

candidates.heading: 10.A Two-Bounce Rule — Fault – No Bounce by Receiver
candidates.content:
10.A.1 Fault – No Bounce by Receiver. When the receiver does not allow
the serve to bounce before hitting the ball, it is a fault against the
receiver.

candidates.heading: 21.A.2 Requesting Time-Out — Fault – Late Time-Out Request
candidates.content:
21.A.2.a Fault – Late Time-Out Request. When a player calls
a time-out after the serve has been hit, it is a fault
against that player.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: 13.E Ball Under Net — Fault – Ball Under Net
candidates.content:
13.E.1 Fault – Ball Under Net. When a player hits the ball under the net, it
is a fault against the player.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: 13.F Ball Crossing Plane of Net — Fault – Ball Hit Before Crossing Plane of Net
candidates.content:
13.F.1 Fault – Ball Hit Before Crossing Plane of Net. When a player hits
the ball before the ball entirely crosses the plane of the net to the
player’s end, it is a fault against the player.

candidates.heading: 5.C.1 Player or Position Error Claimed During Rally — Fault – Incorrect Receiver
candidates.content:
5.C.1.c Fault – Incorrect Receiver. When the correct server
and correct receiver are in their correct positions when
the score is called, it is a fault against a player who
returns the serve but is not the correct receiver, even if
the rally is completed before the fault is called. The
fault must be called before the next serve.

Coaching. Communication of information (including verbal, nonverbal, and
electronic) from someone other than a player’s partner, that players may act upon

Court. The area inside the outer dimensions of the baselines and sidelines.

interfere with the opponent’s ability or concentration to hit the ball. Examples
include, but are not limited to, making loud noises, stomping feet, and
waving the paddle in an erratic manner.
Double Bounce. When the ball bounces twice on one end of the net before it is
returned.

after the ball bounces on the playing surface.

injurious behavioral violation.

injurious behavioral violation.

candidates.heading: Ball Specifications
candidates.content:
3.C Ball Specifications. The requirements for the ball are set forth in Rules 3.C.1
through 3.C.5. The complete list of approved balls is posted on the USA
Pickleball website.

candidates.heading: 3.C Ball Specifications — Design
candidates.content:
3.C.2 Design. The design of the ball must be approved by USA Pickleball
as detailed in the Equipment Standards Manual. USA Pickleball
Equipment Standards Manual

candidates.heading: Ball Selection
candidates.content:
16.G Ball Selection. The Tournament Director will choose the tournament ball
from the official list of approved balls posted on the USA Pickleball website.

candidates.heading: 7.C Volley Serve — Ball Height
candidates.content:
7.C.3 Ball Height. The ball must clearly be no higher than the server’s
waist when the paddle contacts the ball.

candidates.heading: 3.C Ball Specifications — Usage
candidates.content:
3.C.1 Usage. All approved balls are acceptable for indoor or outdoor
play. (See Figure 3-2.)

candidates.heading: 3.C Ball Specifications — Construction
candidates.content:
3.C.5 Construction. The ball must be made of durable material molded
with a smooth surface and free of texturing. The ball may have a
slight ridge at the seam, as long as it does not significantly impact
the ball’s flight characteristics. (See Figure 3-2.)
The ball with larger holes is customarily used
for indoor play (pictured on the left). The ball
with smaller holes is customarily used for
outdoor play (pictured on the right).
Figure 3-2: Approved Balls – Examples

candidates.heading: 7.B Ball Release — Release from Hand or Paddle
candidates.content:
7.B.1 Release from Hand or Paddle. The server must release the ball
using only one hand or only the paddle.

candidates.heading: Extra Ball
candidates.content:
24.B Extra Ball. An extra ball carried by a player during a rally must not be
visible to the opponent and must remain in possession of the player.

candidates.heading: 22.I Match Forfeit by Referee — Dangerous Paddle or Ball Abuse
candidates.content:
22.I.1 Dangerous Paddle or Ball Abuse. Aggressively or recklessly
striking or throwing a ball or paddle in frustration or anger that
strikes an individual or damages facility property.

candidates.heading: 17.D Officiating Play — Damaged Balls
candidates.content:
17.D.14 Damaged Balls. Determine whether a ball is broken or cracked
and must be replaced, and whether the broken or cracked ball
affected the outcome of a rally. (See Rule 20.F.)

candidates.heading: 3.C Ball Specifications — Color
candidates.content:
3.C.3 Color. The ball must be one uniform color, except for identification
markings. Colors may vary.

candidates.heading: Ball Release
candidates.content:
7.B Ball Release. The server must comply with Rules 7.B.1 through 7.B.3 when
releasing the ball to make the serve.

candidates.heading: 20.F Damaged Ball — Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball
candidates.content:
20.F.1 Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball. When the referee determines
that the broken or cracked ball affected the outcome of the rally,
the rally must be replayed with a replacement ball. (Modifies
Rule 10.G.1)

candidates.heading: Damaged Ball
candidates.content:
10.G Damaged Ball. When a ball is or becomes broken, cracked, soft or degraded,
play must continue until the end of the rally. The ball will be replaced if all
players agree.

candidates.heading: 10.G Damaged Ball — No Replay – Soft or Degraded Ball
candidates.content:
10.G.2 No Replay – Soft or Degraded Ball. When a ball is or becomes
degraded or soft, the result of the prior rally stands.

candidates.heading: 22.L Ejection or Expulsion — Injurious Paddle or Ball Abuse
candidates.content:
22.L.2 Injurious Paddle or Ball Abuse. Damage to the venue or injury
to a player, official, or spectator through an act of paddle or ball
abuse or other acts of physical violence.

candidates.heading: 20.E.2 Replays — Replay – Volley Serve, Questionable Ball Height.
candidates.content:
20.E.2.h Replay – Volley Serve, Questionable Ball Height.
When it is questionable whether the ball was no
higher than the server’s waist when the paddle
contacted the ball to make a volley serve, the referee
may call for a replay.

candidates.heading: 25.B.3 Two-Bounce Allowance — Dead Ball
candidates.content:
25.B.3.d Dead Ball. When the ball strikes a permanent object
(e.g., fence, wall) before the second bounce, it is a
dead ball and the rally ends.

candidates.heading: 7.B Ball Release — No Manipulation or Spin Upon Release
candidates.content:
7.B.2 No Manipulation or Spin Upon Release. Some natural rotation of
the ball is expected during any release of the ball. The server must
not manipulate the ball to add spin with any part of the server's
body or the paddle prior to hitting the ball to make the serve,
except that the server may allow the ball to roll off the face of the
paddle by gravity. Spin may be applied to the ball upon contact by
the paddle.

candidates.heading: 10.G Damaged Ball — Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball
candidates.content:
10.G.1 Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball. When all players agree that a
broken or cracked ball affected the outcome of the rally, the rally
must be replayed. If all players do not agree that a broken or
cracked ball affected the outcome of the rally, the result of the rally
stands.

candidates.heading: 20.E.2 Replays — Replay – Drop Serve, Questionable Force on Ball.
candidates.content:
20.E.2.i Replay – Drop Serve, Questionable Force on Ball.
When it is questionable whether the ball was
propelled when the server released the ball to make
a drop serve, the referee must call for a replay.

candidates.heading: USA Pickleball Approved Paddle
candidates.content:
18.A USA Pickleball Approved Paddle. Players must use an approved paddle
that complies with the paddle specifications in Rule 3.D. Players must
confirm that their paddle is approved and listed on the USA Pickleball
Approved Paddle List.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: Ball Around Net Post
candidates.content:
13.C Ball Around Net Post. A ball may be returned around the outside of the net
post.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: Ball Under Net
candidates.content: 13.E Ball Under Net. A ball must not be hit under the net.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: Ball Between Net and Net Post
candidates.content:
13.D Ball Between Net and Net Post. A ball must not be hit between the net and
the net post.

candidates.heading: 22.B Verbal and Technical Warnings — Ball Abuse
candidates.content:
22.B.4 Ball Abuse. Intentionally damaging or aggressively hitting a
dead ball without endangering people.

candidates.heading: Damaged Ball
candidates.content:
20.F Damaged Ball. A player may appeal to the referee to determine whether a
ball is degraded, soft, broken, or cracked. A potentially soft or degraded
ball will not be replaced unless all players agree. If the referee determines
that the ball is broken or cracked, it will be replaced. (Modifies Rule 10.G)

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: Ball Contacting Net Support System
candidates.content:
13.B Ball Contacting Net Support System. A served ball must not contact any
part of the net support system. A returned ball must not contact any part of
the net support system on the hitting player’s end of the net.

candidates.heading: 22.D Technical Fouls — Ball Abuse
candidates.content:
22.D.2 Ball Abuse. Aggressively or recklessly throwing or hitting a dead
ball in frustration or anger with negligent disregard for the
consequences as long as the ball does not strike a person but
puts a person at risk or in danger.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: 13.B Ball Contacting Net Support System — Replay – Ball Affected by Net Support System
candidates.content:
13.B.2 Replay – Ball Affected by Net Support System. When a returned
ball crosses the net and contacts any part of a crossbar, or any
other part of the net support system within the court boundaries,
before or after the ball bounces, the rally must be replayed.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: 13.A Ball Contacting Net — Replay – Ball Contacts Net
candidates.content:
13.A.1 Replay – Ball Contacts Net. When a returned ball that crosses the
net gets caught in the net, contacts a part of the net that is draping
on the ground, or contacts a deflecting net before or after
bouncing, the rally must be replayed.

candidates.heading: Returned Ball Placement
candidates.content:
10.C Returned Ball Placement. A player must return the ball so that the ball
lands on the opponent’s end of the court or contacts the opponent or
anything that is worn or carried by the opponent before the ball lands.

candidates.heading: 17.D Officiating Play — Damaged Balls
candidates.content:
17.D.14 Damaged Balls. Determine whether a ball is broken or cracked
and must be replaced, and whether the broken or cracked ball
affected the outcome of a rally. (See Rule 20.F.)

candidates.heading: 20.F Damaged Ball — Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball
candidates.content:
20.F.1 Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball. When the referee determines
that the broken or cracked ball affected the outcome of the rally,
the rally must be replayed with a replacement ball. (Modifies
Rule 10.G.1)

candidates.heading: 10.C Returned Ball Placement — Fault – Ball Hits Permanent Object After Landing
candidates.content:
10.C.5 Fault – Ball Hits Permanent Object After Landing. When a player
fails to return a ball that has bounced in the player’s court before
the ball contacts a permanent object, it is a fault against that
player.

candidates.heading: 10.G Damaged Ball — Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball
candidates.content:
10.G.1 Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball. When all players agree that a
broken or cracked ball affected the outcome of the rally, the rally
must be replayed. If all players do not agree that a broken or
cracked ball affected the outcome of the rally, the result of the rally
stands.

candidates.heading: 10.G Damaged Ball — No Replay – Soft or Degraded Ball
candidates.content:
10.G.2 No Replay – Soft or Degraded Ball. When a ball is or becomes
degraded or soft, the result of the prior rally stands.

candidates.heading: 10.C Returned Ball Placement — Fault – Ball Hits Player
candidates.content:
10.C.3 Fault – Ball Hits Player. After the serve, when the ball contacts a
player or anything that is worn or carried by the player, except the
player’s paddle or the player’s hands below the wrist joint while in
contact with the paddle, it is a fault against that player.

candidates.heading: 3.C Ball Specifications — Construction
candidates.content:
3.C.5 Construction. The ball must be made of durable material molded
with a smooth surface and free of texturing. The ball may have a
slight ridge at the seam, as long as it does not significantly impact
the ball’s flight characteristics. (See Figure 3-2.)
The ball with larger holes is customarily used
for indoor play (pictured on the left). The ball
with smaller holes is customarily used for
outdoor play (pictured on the right).
Figure 3-2: Approved Balls – Examples

candidates.heading: 10.C Returned Ball Placement — Fault – Ball Hits Permanent Object Before Landing
candidates.content:
10.C.4 Fault – Ball Hits Permanent Object Before Landing. When a
player hits a ball that contacts a permanent object before
bouncing on the court, it is a fault against that player.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 9: Dead Balls, Faults, and Hinders
candidates.heading: 9.B Faults — Fault Occurrence
candidates.content:
9.B.1 Fault Occurrence. A fault only occurs while the ball is live, except
for non-volley zone violations involving momentum. (See Rule
11.A.2.)

candidates.heading: 24.B Extra Ball — Fault – Extra Ball Visible or Ball Falls
candidates.content:
24.B.1 Fault – Extra Ball Visible or Ball Falls. When an extra ball
carried by a player is visible to an opponent or falls to the
playing surface while the ball is live, it is a fault against the
player.

candidates.heading: 25.B.3 Two-Bounce Allowance — Fault – Failure to Return Ball Before Third Bounce.
candidates.content:
25.B.3.c Fault – Failure to Return Ball Before Third Bounce.
When the player does not return a ball before it
bounces three times, it is a fault against the player.
(Modifies Rule 10.B.1.)

candidates.heading: 22.B Verbal and Technical Warnings — Ball Abuse
candidates.content:
22.B.4 Ball Abuse. Intentionally damaging or aggressively hitting a
dead ball without endangering people.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: 13.I.2 Ball Crosses Back to Opponent’s Side — Fault – Ball Not Contacted
candidates.content:
13.I.2.b Fault – Ball Not Contacted. When a ball bounces in
the court on the receiving player’s end of the net and
then returns to the opponent’s end of the net without
being hit, it is a fault against a player who fails to hit
the ball before it bounces once on the opponent’s end
of the net.

candidates.heading: 25.B.3 Two-Bounce Allowance — Dead Ball
candidates.content:
25.B.3.d Dead Ball. When the ball strikes a permanent object
(e.g., fence, wall) before the second bounce, it is a
dead ball and the rally ends.

candidates.heading: 25.A.9 Two-Bounce Allowance — Fault – Failure to Return Ball Before Third Bounce.
candidates.content:
25.A.9.a Fault – Failure to Return Ball Before Third Bounce.
When a wheelchair player does not return a ball
before it bounces three times, it is a fault against the
player. (Modifies Rule 10.B.1)

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: 13.I.1 After Hitting the Ball — Fault – Player Crosses Plane of Net Before Hitting
candidates.content:
13.I.1.a Fault – Player Crosses Plane of Net Before Hitting
Ball. When any part of a player or anything that is worn
or carried by the player crosses the plane of the net
before the player hits the ball, it is a fault against the
player.

candidates.heading: Returned Ball Placement
candidates.content:
10.C Returned Ball Placement. A player must return the ball so that the ball
lands on the opponent’s end of the court or contacts the opponent or
anything that is worn or carried by the opponent before the ball lands.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: 13.E Ball Under Net — Fault – Ball Under Net
candidates.content:
13.E.1 Fault – Ball Under Net. When a player hits the ball under the net, it
is a fault against the player.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: 13.G Player Contacting Net or Net Support System — Fault – Player Contacts Net or Net Support System
candidates.content:
13.G.1 Fault – Player Contacts Net or Net Support System. When a
player or anything that is worn or carried by the player contacts the
net or net support system while the ball is live, it is a fault against
the player.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: Ball Contacting Net
candidates.content:
13.A Ball Contacting Net. When the ball contacts the net, or the rope or cable at
the top of the net between the net posts, the ball remains in play.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: Ball Contacting Net Support System
candidates.content:
13.B Ball Contacting Net Support System. A served ball must not contact any
part of the net support system. A returned ball must not contact any part of
the net support system on the hitting player’s end of the net.

candidates.heading: 10.D Double Hit — Fault – Ball Hit by Two-Players
candidates.content:
10.D.2 Fault – Ball Hit by Two-Players. It is a fault if both a player and
their partner strike the ball while attempting to return it.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: 13.I.1 After Hitting the Ball — Fault – Player Crosses Plane of Net Without Hitting
candidates.content:
13.I.1.b Fault – Player Crosses Plane of Net Without Hitting
Ball. When any part of a player or anything that is worn
or carried by the player crosses the plane of the net
and the player does not hit the ball, it is a fault against
the player.

candidates.heading: 10.C Returned Ball Placement — Fault – Ball Lands Out of Bounds
candidates.content:
10.C.1 Fault – Ball Lands Out of Bounds. When a player hits a ball that
first lands outside the opponent’s end of the court, it is a fault
against that player.

candidates.heading: 10.C Returned Ball Placement — Fault – Ball Lands on Player’s Side of Net
candidates.content:
10.C.2 Fault – Ball Lands on Player’s Side of Net. When a player hits a
ball that fails to cross the net and lands on the player’s side of the
net, it is a fault against that player.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: 13.F Ball Crossing Plane of Net — Fault – Ball Hit Before Crossing Plane of Net
candidates.content:
13.F.1 Fault – Ball Hit Before Crossing Plane of Net. When a player hits
the ball before the ball entirely crosses the plane of the net to the
player’s end, it is a fault against the player.

candidates.heading: Extra Ball
candidates.content:
24.B Extra Ball. An extra ball carried by a player during a rally must not be
visible to the opponent and must remain in possession of the player.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 9: Dead Balls, Faults, and Hinders
candidates.heading: Faults
candidates.content: 9.B Faults. A called fault or a fault committed by a player results in a dead ball.

candidates.heading: Item on Court
candidates.content:
10.J Item on Court. When anything that is worn or carried by a player lands on
the player’s end of the court (except when the item contacts the non-volley
zone as a result of the player volleying the ball (see Rule 11.A.1)), the ball
remains in play, even if the ball hits the item.

candidates.heading: 22.D Technical Fouls — Ball Abuse
candidates.content:
22.D.2 Ball Abuse. Aggressively or recklessly throwing or hitting a dead
ball in frustration or anger with negligent disregard for the
consequences as long as the ball does not strike a person but
puts a person at risk or in danger.

suppliedEvidence.heading: Damaged Ball
suppliedEvidence.content:
10.G Damaged Ball. When a ball is or becomes broken, cracked, soft or degraded,
play must continue until the end of the rally. The ball will be replaced if all
players agree.

suppliedEvidence.heading: Damaged Ball
suppliedEvidence.content:
20.F Damaged Ball. A player may appeal to the referee to determine whether a
ball is degraded, soft, broken, or cracked. A potentially soft or degraded
ball will not be replaced unless all players agree. If the referee determines
that the ball is broken or cracked, it will be replaced. (Modifies Rule 10.G)

17.D.14 Damaged Balls. Determine whether a ball is broken or cracked
and must be replaced, and whether the broken or cracked ball
affected the outcome of a rally. (See Rule 20.F.)

candidates.content:
3.C.3 Color. The ball must be one uniform color, except for identification
markings. Colors may vary.

candidates.heading: Ball Specifications
candidates.content:
3.C Ball Specifications. The requirements for the ball are set forth in Rules 3.C.1
through 3.C.5. The complete list of approved balls is posted on the USA
Pickleball website.

candidates.heading: 3.C Ball Specifications — Usage
candidates.content:
3.C.1 Usage. All approved balls are acceptable for indoor or outdoor
play. (See Figure 3-2.)

candidates.heading: Ball Selection
candidates.content:
16.G Ball Selection. The Tournament Director will choose the tournament ball
from the official list of approved balls posted on the USA Pickleball website.

candidates.heading: Damaged Ball
candidates.content:

ball is degraded, soft, broken, or cracked. A potentially soft or degraded
ball will not be replaced unless all players agree. If the referee determines
that the ball is broken or cracked, it will be replaced. (Modifies Rule 10.G)

24.B Extra Ball. An extra ball carried by a player during a rally must not be
visible to the opponent and must remain in possession of the player.

candidates.heading: 3.C Ball Specifications — Brand Identification
candidates.content:
3.C.4 Brand Identification. The ball must have a manufacturer or
supplier name or logo printed or embossed on the surface.

candidates.heading: 3.C Ball Specifications — Design
candidates.content:
3.C.2 Design. The design of the ball must be approved by USA Pickleball
as detailed in the Equipment Standards Manual. USA Pickleball
Equipment Standards Manual

candidates.heading: 17.D Officiating Play — Damaged Balls
candidates.content:
17.D.14 Damaged Balls. Determine whether a ball is broken or cracked
and must be replaced, and whether the broken or cracked ball
affected the outcome of a rally. (See Rule 20.F.)

candidates.heading: 3.A.4 Lines and Areas — Line Size and Color
candidates.content:
3.A.4.e Line Size and Color. All lines should be 2 inches (5.08
cm) wide and the same color, clearly contrasting with
the color of the playing surface and court.

candidates.heading: 22.B Verbal and Technical Warnings — Ball Abuse
candidates.content:
22.B.4 Ball Abuse. Intentionally damaging or aggressively hitting a
dead ball without endangering people.

candidates.heading: Ball Release
candidates.content:
7.B Ball Release. The server must comply with Rules 7.B.1 through 7.B.3 when
releasing the ball to make the serve.

candidates.heading: 7.C Volley Serve — Ball Height
candidates.content:
7.C.3 Ball Height. The ball must clearly be no higher than the server’s
waist when the paddle contacts the ball.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: Ball Contacting Net Support System
candidates.content:
13.B Ball Contacting Net Support System. A served ball must not contact any
part of the net support system. A returned ball must not contact any part of
the net support system on the hitting player’s end of the net.

candidates.heading: 7.B Ball Release — Visible Release
candidates.content:
7.B.3 Visible Release. The server’s release of the ball must be visible to
the receiver.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: Ball Around Net Post
candidates.content:
13.C Ball Around Net Post. A ball may be returned around the outside of the net
post.

candidates.heading: Damaged Ball
candidates.content:
10.G Damaged Ball. When a ball is or becomes broken, cracked, soft or degraded,
play must continue until the end of the rally. The ball will be replaced if all
players agree.

candidates.content:

ball in frustration or anger with negligent disregard for the
consequences as long as the ball does not strike a person but
puts a person at risk or in danger.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: Ball Crossing Plane of Net
candidates.content:
13.F Ball Crossing Plane of Net. A ball must entirely cross to a player’s end of
the net before the player hits the ball.

candidates.heading: 24.B Extra Ball — Fault – Extra Ball Visible or Ball Falls
candidates.content:
24.B.1 Fault – Extra Ball Visible or Ball Falls. When an extra ball
carried by a player is visible to an opponent or falls to the
playing surface while the ball is live, it is a fault against the
player.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: 13.I Player Crossing Plane of Net — Ball Crosses Back to Opponent’s Side
candidates.content:
13.I.2 Ball Crosses Back to Opponent’s Side. When a ball bounces in the
court on the receiving player’s end of the net and then returns to
the opponent’s side of the net without being hit, the receiving
player may cross over, under, or around the net to hit the ball, but
only after the ball has first crossed back to the opponent’s end of
the net.

candidates.heading: “In” Ball
candidates.content:
8.B “In” Ball. A served ball that clears the opponent’s non-volley zone line and
lands in the correct service court is “in.” A ball returned by a player that
lands on the opponent’s end of the court is “in.”

candidates.heading: 7.B.3 Visible Release — Replay – Ball Release Not Visible
candidates.content:
7.B.3.a Replay – Ball Release Not Visible. When the receiver
cannot see the release of the ball, the receiver may call
for a replay, but only before the return of serve.

candidates.heading: Returned Ball Placement
candidates.content:
10.C Returned Ball Placement. A player must return the ball so that the ball
lands on the opponent’s end of the court or contacts the opponent or
anything that is worn or carried by the opponent before the ball lands.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: Ball Under Net
candidates.content: 13.E Ball Under Net. A ball must not be hit under the net.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: Ball Between Net and Net Post
candidates.content:
13.D Ball Between Net and Net Post. A ball must not be hit between the net and
the net post.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: Ball Contacting Net
candidates.content:
13.A Ball Contacting Net. When the ball contacts the net, or the rope or cable at
the top of the net between the net posts, the ball remains in play.

candidates.heading: 20.E.2 Replays — Replay – Ball Release Not Visible
candidates.content:
20.E.2.a Replay – Ball Release Not Visible. When it is
questionable whether the release of the ball was not
visible to the referee and receiver, the referee may
call for a replay. When the referee is certain that the
release of the ball was not visible, the referee must
call for a replay.

candidates.heading: 20.F Damaged Ball — Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball
candidates.content:
20.F.1 Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball. When the referee determines
that the broken or cracked ball affected the outcome of the rally,
the rally must be replayed with a replacement ball. (Modifies
Rule 10.G.1)

candidates.heading: 10.G Damaged Ball — No Replay – Soft or Degraded Ball
candidates.content:
10.G.2 No Replay – Soft or Degraded Ball. When a ball is or becomes
degraded or soft, the result of the prior rally stands.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: 13.B Ball Contacting Net Support System — Replay – Ball Affected by Net Support System
candidates.content:
13.B.2 Replay – Ball Affected by Net Support System. When a returned
ball crosses the net and contacts any part of a crossbar, or any
other part of the net support system within the court boundaries,
before or after the ball bounces, the rally must be replayed.

candidates.content:
5. TEAM/GAME RULES
5.1. Team Home Court Expectations: All teams registering for league play are expected to
host their share of scheduled home matches by providing adequate court availability,
resulting in a balanced home-and-away schedule whenever possible. If a team cannot
reserve enough courts for all its assigned home match dates, additional matches may be
scheduled as away games. Teams that are unable to provide any courts due to limitations
within their community or facility will play all their scheduled matches as away games.
5.2. Governing Rules & Equipment Standards: All matches are governed by USA Pickleball
Rules (https://usapickleball.org/) and equipment standards including USA Pickleball
approved equipment. In the event of a conflict, specific Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club
(LWR PC) rules shall take precedence over the corresponding USA Pickleball rules and
regulations.
5.3. Unauthorized Equipment Penalty: Games played with unauthorized paddles or
equipment will be forfeited, not recorded, and not posted to DUPR if discovered by
players/captains during or after play.
5.4. Match Setup and Roster Exchange: Home and visiting Captains must submit their
upcoming match rosters through the League Management System (LMS) using the Match
Setup button no later than three (3) days prior to the scheduled match. It is strongly
recommended that the Home Team submit its lineup first. Automated reminder emails
will be sent to all Captains. Any lineup or roster changes made after the initial submission
must be entered through Match Setup, which will automatically notify the opposing
Captain(s) of the change. Teams that have not completed Match Setup will not be able to

candidates.heading: ENTER/VERIFY SCORES
candidates.content:
 Entering Match Scores: To enter scores, click the Enter Match Scores button in the
match. This option becomes available only on or after the scheduled match date and
will be red.
 Forfeits and Weather Delays: If an entire match date is forfeited or canceled due to
weather, notify League Management. They will log the information for that match and
update the standings.
 Score Entry Process: When entering scores, use the dropdown menus to select the
players for each game (built from your Match Setup), then enter the scores in each
game block. Click Submit when finished; the system will check for errors before saving.
 Score Verification: Once scores are submitted, the opposing captain will receive an
email request to verify them, and a red notification count will appear in their Pending
Match Verifications block. The opposing captain must open the match, review the
scores, and click the verification button (or dispute button if they don’t accept the
scores as written). Both captains will then be notified, and the standings will update
automatically.
o The visiting team captain must verify match scores promptly. This ensures there is enough time
to review the results and enter them into DUPR before the end of the weekend.

candidates.heading: 25.C Hybrid Doubles Play — Adaptive Standing Players
candidates.content:
25.C.3 Adaptive Standing Players. Eligible adaptive standing players
(per Rule 25.B.3.a) are the only standing players who may use
the two-bounce allowance in hybrid play and must declare this
accommodation before the match.
Appendix B Rulebook Priorities and Guiding
Principles
Preface
The USA Pickleball Official Rulebook is the organization’s most important product.
It is the foundational document for the sport of pickleball and should be treated
with the respect accorded the sport’s founders and those who have written and
approved rules over the years.
Writing rules that are objective, clear, and concise is difficult work. Because those
involved in writing and/or approving rules come from diverse backgrounds and
experiences, it is important to have rule writing priorities and guiding principles
that help provide a measure of consistency from year to year. The following
Rulebook Priorities and Guiding Principles were developed to guide rule writers and
approvers in their important work.
Priorities
The following three priorities should be considered “tests” for any suggested rule
change. Any suggested rule change should satisfy at least one of these three
priorities, listed in order of importance:
1. The first priority is preserving the integrity of the sport, one that incorporates
the elements of fun, cooperation, courtesy, and competition. This priority pays
homage to those who developed the sport in 1965 and those who have written
and approved rule changes over the years.
2. The second priority is what is collectively best for the players. This priority
examines rule changes for improving the player’s experience. It “tests”
suggested rule changes from the standpoint of minimizing player
disagreements, making it easier to learn the sport, teach the sport, and play
the sport, while also allowing for moderate innovation as player skills and
equipment develop and evolve.
3. The third priority is what is best for officiating. It “tests” rule changes to make it
less likely conflicts will occur between players as well as between players and
officials.
Guiding Principles
The USA Pickleball Official Rulebook contains a wide variety of rules that cover the
court and equipment, recreational and social play as well as tournament play,
officiated and non-officiated. The following are Guiding Principles for those writing
and approving rules. To the extent possible, rules should:
1. Apply to all levels and categories of players: recreational and social players, as
well as professional and amateur tournament players (officiated and non-
officiated). Specific rules for a single category of player, for example, the pro
level player, should be approved after careful consideration and examination
of how the rule change might impact the sport beyond the pro level of
competition.
2. Be written with a deterministic focus, i.e., from the standpoint of “if this occurs,
this is what happens.” If something is not allowed or should not happen, the
consequences (for example: replay, fault, technical warning, etc.) should be
provided as part of the rule (e.g., replay, fault, technical warning, etc.).
3. Center on that which should not occur, not on what is permitted or allowed.
Attempts to include rules describing what is allowed will result in an
unnecessarily lengthy Rulebook.
4. Avoid ambiguity, player discretion, or referee judgment-related rules. Such
rules invite disagreements and different interpretations. To this end, when a
key word is used to describe when a rule applies, the word should be defined
as either a part of the rule or in the Definition section of the Rulebook.
5. Allow equipment manufacturers to innovate, as long as such innovation does
not overwhelm or outpace the average player’s ability to keep up with the
speed and difficulty of the sport. Equipment-related rule changes should be
given particularly close scrutiny because of their precedent-setting potential.
6. Have an element of precedent accorded to them. Change for change’s sake
should be avoided to avoid frustration among, or a loss of confidence by,
players.
7. Allow for an appropriate degree of player innovation. Such innovation should
maintain a healthy balance between historical rules that have been
instrumental to the sport’s growth and appeal.
8. Preserve the unique features and rules of the sport involving the Non-Volley
Zone and the two-bounce rule and prevent one shot, one paddle, or one type
of play from dominating the sport.
9. Address a known issue or anticipate trends and needs of the sport before
problems develop.
10. Be subjected to reviews and comments by domestic and international
stakeholders.

candidates.heading: Definitions
candidates.content:
Section 2 Definitions
Ball In Play. The timeframe during which a rally is played, from when the serve is
hit until the ball becomes dead.
Carry. Hitting the ball in such a way that it does not bounce away from the paddle
but is carried along on the face of the paddle.
Coaching. Communication of information (including verbal, nonverbal, and
electronic) from someone other than a player’s partner, that players may act upon
to gain an advantage or help them avoid a rules violation.
Court. The area inside the outer dimensions of the baselines and sidelines.
Dead Ball. A ball that is no longer in play.
Distraction. Physical actions by a player that are not common to the game and
interfere with the opponent’s ability or concentration to hit the ball. Examples
include, but are not limited to, making loud noises, stomping feet, and
waving the paddle in an erratic manner.
Double Bounce. When the ball bounces twice on one end of the net before it is
returned.
Double Hit. Hitting the ball twice before it is returned.
Drop Serve. A serve made by dropping the ball and hitting the ball with the paddle
after the ball bounces on the playing surface.
Ejection. Removal of a player from tournament competition for a flagrant or
injurious behavioral violation.
Expulsion. Banishment of a player from the tournament venue for a flagrant or
injurious behavioral violation.
Fault. A rules violation that results in a dead ball and the loss of a rally.
First Server (Doubles). The player who begins the team’s service rotation from
the right serving area after a side out.
Forfeit. The awarding of a game or a match to the opponent due to a violation of
the rules.
Hinder. Any transient element or occurrence not caused by a player that adversely
impacts play. Examples include, but are not limited to, stray balls, flying insects,

candidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
candidates.heading: Scheduling
candidates.content:
6.1.1. Scheduling: Games are typically scheduled for Wednesdays at noon for women
and Thursdays at noon for men. DUPR 9: See 6.1.9 below.
6.1.2. Roster & Courts: 6 Players / 3 Lines. Requires 3 courts.
6.1.3. Match Format: Round robin; one game to 15, win by 1. Each team receives two
one-minute timeouts. Teams switch ends when the first team reaches 8 points,
and visitors choose serve, receive, side, or defer in games 1 and 3.

candidates.heading: 23.B Withdrawal from Bracket — Withdrawal Before Start of Bracket
candidates.content:
23.B.1 Withdrawal Before Start of Bracket. A singles player or
doubles team may withdraw from a bracket that has not started
play.

Viewing My Teams Information
If you are on multiple teams, you can easily switch between them. Go to the sidebar, select
My Team, and choose the team you want to see.
The team page displays:
• Next Match: Shows at the top with quick links to Match Details and Match Lineup
(if available).
• Team Performance: Displays your team's current record, rank and your personal
season DUPR rating.
• Schedules & Results: Lists of upcoming matches and recent match results.
• Team Roster: Shows your full roster. Tap or click any captain's card to email them
directly.
• League Documents: Access all current league files via the sidebar option.
For more details, see the sections below on Team Roster, Division Standings, and Team
Matches.

candidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club Code of Conduct
candidates.content:
1. Standard of Play & Sportsmanship
• Golden Rule: Treat every player, regardless of skill level, with the same respect you
expect to receive.
• Positive Environment: Support your partners and remain respectful to your
opponents. Avoid "trash talk" that crosses the line into being mean-spirited or
discouraging.
• Integrity of the Game: Players must make line calls that are "clear and certain." In
accordance with standard pickleball officiating, all "close" calls must be resolved in
favor of the opponent.
• Player Integrity: Any attempt to manipulate ratings through "sandbagging,"
reporting false scores, or intentionally losing matches is strictly prohibited and
grounds for immediate expulsion.
• On-Court Decorum: Profanity, paddle throwing, or aggressive physical gestures
toward opponents, partners, or spectators will not be tolerated.

candidates.heading: 21.C Medical Time-Out — Time Start
candidates.content:
21.C.7 Time Start. When medical assistance arrives, the referee will
start a 15-minute timer. Play must resume as soon as possible
but no later than 15 minutes of elapsed time.

suppliedEvidence.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR Captains Guide
suppliedEvidence.heading: CREATE/UPDATE TEAM ROSTER
suppliedEvidence.content:
CREATE/UPDATE TEAM ROSTER
o Enter or update your player team roster prior to the commencement of each season. Use the
Manage Roster option to add or remove players.
 All players must be active Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club members before playing. To
join, they can visit: https://lwrpickleballclub.com/signup.
 All DUPR League players must have a free DUPR ID which can be created at
https://www.dupr.com.
 All players must join the Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club DUPR club (free and
separate from the LWR PC membership) so we can accurately sync player ratings.
Captains should share this link with all players: https://tinyurl.com/LWRPC-DUPRCLUB.
o Roster Requirements & Substitutes: Teams must roster enough players and substitutes (who
are not already on another team) to field a full lineup weekly. For example, if your match
requires 6 players, an 8–10 player roster is recommended. Additional substitutes may be drawn
from other teams in the same community, provided they meet the DUPR division rating
requirements. For complete details, see the Player Requirements and DUPR Rating/Divisions
sections in the DUPR League Mission and Rules.
o Captain Roster Control: Captains are responsible for building their own rosters and may add
or delete players throughout the season as needed provided the player is a current, valid
member of the LWR PC, has a DUPR ID and is eligible for that division.
o Player DUPR Ratings: Season DUPR ratings are updated in the LMS before the season starts
and remain visible to captains all season. For players added midseason, their rating is based on
the date the league's season ratings were originally recorded.

suppliedEvidence.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
suppliedEvidence.heading: TEAM/GAME RULES
suppliedEvidence.content:
5. TEAM/GAME RULES
5.1. Team Home Court Expectations: All teams registering for league play are expected to
host their share of scheduled home matches by providing adequate court availability,
resulting in a balanced home-and-away schedule whenever possible. If a team cannot
reserve enough courts for all its assigned home match dates, additional matches may be
scheduled as away games. Teams that are unable to provide any courts due to limitations
within their community or facility will play all their scheduled matches as away games.
5.2. Governing Rules & Equipment Standards: All matches are governed by USA Pickleball
Rules (https://usapickleball.org/) and equipment standards including USA Pickleball
approved equipment. In the event of a conflict, specific Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club
(LWR PC) rules shall take precedence over the corresponding USA Pickleball rules and
regulations.
5.3. Unauthorized Equipment Penalty: Games played with unauthorized paddles or
equipment will be forfeited, not recorded, and not posted to DUPR if discovered by
players/captains during or after play.
5.4. Match Setup and Roster Exchange: Home and visiting Captains must submit their
upcoming match rosters through the League Management System (LMS) using the Match
Setup button no later than three (3) days prior to the scheduled match. It is strongly
recommended that the Home Team submit its lineup first. Automated reminder emails
will be sent to all Captains. Any lineup or roster changes made after the initial submission
must be entered through Match Setup, which will automatically notify the opposing
Captain(s) of the change. Teams that have not completed Match Setup will not be able to
print a completed Match Score Sheet. Repeated failure to complete Match Setup within

intentDiagnostic.evidenceMatch: Concrete timing requirement in numbered rule

suppliedEvidence.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR Captains Guide
suppliedEvidence.heading: ENTER/VERIFY SCORES
suppliedEvidence.content:
 Entering Match Scores: To enter scores, click the Enter Match Scores button in the
match. This option becomes available only on or after the scheduled match date and
will be red.
 Forfeits and Weather Delays: If an entire match date is forfeited or canceled due to
weather, notify League Management. They will log the information for that match and
update the standings.
 Score Entry Process: When entering scores, use the dropdown menus to select the
players for each game (built from your Match Setup), then enter the scores in each
game block. Click Submit when finished; the system will check for errors before saving.
 Score Verification: Once scores are submitted, the opposing captain will receive an
email request to verify them, and a red notification count will appear in their Pending
Match Verifications block. The opposing captain must open the match, review the
scores, and click the verification button (or dispute button if they don’t accept the
scores as written). Both captains will then be notified, and the standings will update
automatically.
o The visiting team captain must verify match scores promptly. This ensures there is enough time
to review the results and enter them into DUPR before the end of the weekend.

Match Setup Process
Captains must assign player pairings and save their lineups before the match date. To
ensure fair play, the system automatically checks entries against division ranges, team
totals, and Season DUPR ratings, displaying an on-screen warning if a combination is
ineligible. It is highly recommended that the Home Team enter their lineup first. Lineups
can be changed prior to match day with all changes automatically emailed to opposing
captains.
• In Match Setup, roster choices are filtered against the division’s configured rating
type: Season DUPR, or Age-based/PrimeTime (season_primetime_rating). Players
with no valid rating or outside the division minimum/maximum cannot be selected.
It also checks the two-player combined rating cap.
• Before saving, it refreshes the season ratings and validates again. The save API
repeats that validation server-side, including roster membership, individual rating
range, duplicates, and team-rating maximum.
The rating source is selected by the division’s rating_type: standard divisions use Season
DUPR; PrimeTime/Age-based divisions use the Season PrimeTime rating.
The Match Setup button will show as red if your setup is incomplete, and blue once it is
completed. When both teams have completed their setup, the Match Score Sheet button
will turn green, allowing you to print a complete match score sheet.
Saving a lineup (press the Save Match Setup button) automatically notifies the opposing
captain of the update. From this screen, you can also use the Email Players button to notify
all selected players or the entire team.
For any questions regarding player ratings or eligibility, contact
info@lwrpickleballclub.com.

Season DUPR Ratings of both players. Each division has established minimum and
maximum individual player ratings, as well as a maximum combined Team DUPR
Rating. These limits are strictly enforced.
4.6.1. Every lineup fielded for a match must comply with both the individual player rating
requirements and the maximum combined Team DUPR Rating for that division.
Teams that fail to meet these requirements will automatically forfeit the aƯected
games.

authorityReviewCandidates.content:
Submitting Scores
Clicking Submit Scores saves the match results only when all player, team, and score
information is valid according to division rules. You cannot save any of the results (partial
save) if any information is invalid.
Once submitted:
• Notifications: The system automatically emails the opposing captains to notify
them that the scores have been entered.
• Verification: If your team is the first to enter the results, a captain of the opposing
team must log in to verify or dispute the scores to finalize the match and update the
league/division standings.
Score Verification Process
Use Pending Verification to review entered scores or raise disputes.
Selecting the appropriate button will:
• Finalize Results: Complete the scoring process for the match.
• Notify Captains: Automatically email all captains to confirm the match date and
scores are officially entered and locked.

authorityReviewCandidates.content:
18.G Partner Change (Doubles). With the Tournament Director’s approval, a
player may change a partner before a first-round match when the change is
due to injury, illness, or circumstances beyond the control of the player. A
partner change after the partners start team play is prohibited.

authorityReviewCandidates.heading: Roster Continuity
authorityReviewCandidates.content:
5.13.3. Roster Continuity: When a game is rescheduled, the players originally assigned to
it must participate and maintain their original positions/line assignments.
5.14. End of Season PlayoƯs/Championship Day (All Leagues)
5.14.1. Teams starting the season with fewer scheduled games than others in their
Division/Pool will receive compensatory points at the end of the season. These
points will be calculated based on the team’s average points earned per match
date, rounded to the nearest whole number (0.5 and above rounds up; 0.4 and
below rounds down).

5.5. Roster Requirements & Retroactive Additions: All active players must appear on the
team’s roster in the LMS prior to match play. Retroactive additions are permitted without
penalty only if the player is a valid LWR PC member with an eligible DUPR account and
rating. Failure to meet these requirements will result in a match forfeit, and the match will
not be posted to DUPR.
5.6. DUPR Submission & Eligibility: All qualifying games will be automatically entered into
the DUPR rating system. Games that are forfeited, incomplete, or deemed ineligible will
not be recorded in DUPR (unless otherwise specified by a rule). Individuals/Players are
not authorized to independently submit any Club League scheduled games to DUPR.
5.7. Incomplete Matches: Forfeits vs. Retirements: If a player cannot complete a match for
any reason, the scoring and DUPR eligibility depend on the current score:
5.7.1. Under 6 Points (Forfeit): If neither team has reached 6 points, the match is a
Forfeit, recorded as 0-0, and excluded from DUPR.
5.7.2. 6+ Points (Retired): If at least one team has 6 or more points, the match is recorded
as Retired. Current scores are entered, and results will be posted to DUPR.
5.7.3. Note: In both scenarios, the opposing team is credited with the win. A substitute
may fill in for any remaining games in the session; however, any games left unplayed
without a substitute will be marked as forfeited.
5.8. Coaching & Court Access: Coaching is permitted only during timeouts or between
games. Coaches and non-players must always remain oƯ the court; only active players
may be on the courts.

2. Respect for Host Communities
As a decentralized league, LWR PC relies on the goodwill of local communities.
• Facility Stewardship: Club Members must respect the specific rules of the
community providing the courts (e.g., parking regulations, noise ordinances, and
guest policies).
• Neutrality: Club Members are guests in these communities. Any behavior that
jeopardizes LWR PC’s relationship with a host community is considered a Level 2
violation.

candidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
candidates.heading: PLAYER REQUIREMENTS
candidates.content:
3. PLAYER REQUIREMENTS
3.1. All League players must have a signed/accepted waiver with LWR PC and have a valid
LWR PC membership. To sign up, go to https://lwrpickleballclub.com/signup/.
3.2. All DUPR League players must have a free DUPR ID which can be found at:
https://www.dupr.com/.
3.3. All DUPR League players must join our free DUPR club, which is diƯerent/separate from
the LWR PC membership: https://tinyurl.com/LWRPC-DUPRCLUB
3.4. Players are assigned to a community based on their primary address at the start of the
season.
3.5. Players may form teams with members from other communities; however, they are not
permitted to play for another community’s team if their own community already has a
team in their division.
3.6. Captains are expected to prioritize players from the local community ahead of those from
outside the community. As a community-based league, we emphasize the inclusion of
local players over non-local players.
3.7. Players are permitted to join or substitute for multiple community teams within the same
community, provided that all League and DUPR rating regulations are adhered to.
3.8. Players must be at least 19 years old.
3.9. Players are responsible for verifying their paddle is on the current Approved Paddle List
(https://equipment.usapickleball.org/paddle-list/).

holds final authority on all league disputes, roster eligibility, and rule interpretations.

at the discretion of the Commissioner and/or League Manager and must be
supported by valid LWR PC data via signed score sheets or other comparable hard
documentation.

Manage Roster option to add or remove players.

member of the LWR PC, has a DUPR ID and is eligible for that division.
o Player DUPR Ratings: Season DUPR ratings are updated in the LMS before the season starts
and remain visible to captains all season. For players added midseason, their rating is based on
the date the league's season ratings were originally recorded.
