nor shall they influence any calls or decisions on the court.
5.10. Video Recording: Video recording is allowed only if all players give their approval before
the game starts.
5.11. Rescheduling & Score Submission Deadlines: If both coaches agree, games may be
rescheduled to a diƯerent time on the same day or to another day within the same week.
However, all game scores must be submitted by the end of Sunday of the same week by
midnight. If this deadline cannot be met due to weather conditions or other unforeseen
circumstances, the Home Captain must notify info@lwrpickleballclub.com before
Sunday at midnight with the rescheduled date and time. Failure to do so may result in
forfeiture of the games.
5.12. Makeup Game Deadline: All makeup games must be played at least one week before the
playoƯs/championship date.
5.13. Weather Interruptions & Mid-Match Stoppages: If weather or other factors interrupt
play after a match has started, the following rules apply based on progress:
5.13.1. Less than half of the games completed: Remaining games should be
rescheduled. Only fully completed games will count toward final scores;
unfinished or unplayed games will not be recorded.
5.13.2. At least half of the games are completed: Completed results will stand. Any
remaining unplayed games may be either rescheduled or canceled as agreed upon
by both Captains (rescheduling is the preferred option).

candidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
candidates.heading: TEAM/GAME RULES
candidates.content:
5. TEAM/GAME RULES
5.1. Team Home Court Expectations: All teams registering for league play are expected to
host their share of scheduled home matches by providing adequate court availability,
resulting in a balanced home-and-away schedule whenever possible. If a team cannot
reserve enough courts for all its assigned home match dates, additional matches may be
scheduled as away games. Teams that are unable to provide any courts due to limitations
within their community or facility will play all their scheduled matches as away games.
5.2. Governing Rules & Equipment Standards: All matches are governed by USA Pickleball
Rules (https://usapickleball.org/) and equipment standards including USA Pickleball
approved equipment. In the event of a conflict, specific Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club
(LWR PC) rules shall take precedence over the corresponding USA Pickleball rules and
regulations.
5.3. Unauthorized Equipment Penalty: Games played with unauthorized paddles or
equipment will be forfeited, not recorded, and not posted to DUPR if discovered by
players/captains during or after play.
5.4. Match Setup and Roster Exchange: Home and visiting Captains must submit their
upcoming match rosters through the League Management System (LMS) using the Match
Setup button no later than three (3) days prior to the scheduled match. It is strongly
recommended that the Home Team submit its lineup first. Automated reminder emails
will be sent to all Captains. Any lineup or roster changes made after the initial submission
must be entered through Match Setup, which will automatically notify the opposing
Captain(s) of the change. Teams that have not completed Match Setup will not be able to

candidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
candidates.heading: DUPR RATINGS/DIVISIONS
candidates.content:
4. DUPR RATINGS/DIVISIONS
4.1. Season DUPR Ratings: A player's Season DUPR Rating is established on the date
communicated to all captains prior to the first scheduled league match and remains in
eƯect for the duration of the season.
4.1.1. A player with a DUPR Reliability Factor below 29 will be classified as “Not Rated”
(NR) for League purposes and will be subject to the provisions of Rule 4.5. This
classification recognizes that a player’s current DUPR rating may not yet provide a
suƯiciently reliable indication of skill level, particularly for newer or less-established
players or those who have not recently recorded matches in DUPR. Players
classified as “NR” may be placed on a team in the division that most appropriately
reflects their current skill level while they record additional matches and establish a
more reliable DUPR rating. These players are strongly encouraged to consult with a
local Certified DUPR Coach, pickleball professional, or knowledgeable team
captain for guidance regarding appropriate division placement.
4.2. All DUPR ratings will be truncated to the nearest tenth to establish a player's “Season's
DUPR Rating”. For example, a rating of 3.496 will be truncated to 3.4, as will a rating of
3.401.
4.3. Some of our Leagues use the “Age-based” DUPR sub-rating but will still follow all DUPR
Rating/Division Rules. If a player hasn’t established their 65+ Age-based rating as of the
start of a season, their 50+ Age-based rating will be used.
4.4. Any player or team that is found to be cheating, tanking, game-fixing or any kind of data
manipulation, including intentionally creating multiple DUPR accounts, will be banned
from the League for one calendar year.
4.5. Players with a DUPR Rating of "NR" (Not Rated): Players with a DUPR rating of NR (Not

candidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
candidates.heading: DUPR RATINGS/DIVISIONS
candidates.content:
Rated) are eligible to participate in any division. However, it is strongly recommended that
a Certified DUPR Coach or qualified pickleball professional provide input to help
determine the player's most appropriate skill level. The team captain is ultimately
responsible for ensuring the player is placed in the proper division to promote balanced
and fair competition for all teams.
4.5.1. For team aggregate rating calculations, an NR player will initially be assigned a
Season DUPR Rating equal to the maximum individual DUPR rating allowed for
that division, minus 0.5. For example, in a division, where the maximum individual
rating is 3.8, an NR player would be assigned an initial Season DUPR Rating of 3.3
(3.8 − 0.5) for team aggregate calculations.
4.5.2. If a player is rostered on teams in multiple divisions, the highest adjusted Season
DUPR Rating assigned to that player will be used consistently across all divisions in
which they appear.

Match Setup Process
Captains must assign player pairings and save their lineups before the match date. To
ensure fair play, the system automatically checks entries against division ranges, team
totals, and Season DUPR ratings, displaying an on-screen warning if a combination is
ineligible. It is highly recommended that the Home Team enter their lineup first. Lineups
can be changed prior to match day with all changes automatically emailed to opposing
captains.
• In Match Setup, roster choices are filtered against the division’s configured rating
type: Season DUPR, or Age-based/PrimeTime (season_primetime_rating). Players
with no valid rating or outside the division minimum/maximum cannot be selected.
It also checks the two-player combined rating cap.
• Before saving, it refreshes the season ratings and validates again. The save API
repeats that validation server-side, including roster membership, individual rating
range, duplicates, and team-rating maximum.
The rating source is selected by the division’s rating_type: standard divisions use Season
DUPR; PrimeTime/Age-based divisions use the Season PrimeTime rating.
The Match Setup button will show as red if your setup is incomplete, and blue once it is
completed. When both teams have completed their setup, the Match Score Sheet button
will turn green, allowing you to print a complete match score sheet.
Saving a lineup (press the Save Match Setup button) automatically notifies the opposing
captain of the update. From this screen, you can also use the Email Players button to notify
all selected players or the entire team.
For any questions regarding player ratings or eligibility, contact
info@lwrpickleballclub.com.
Match Setup Window

standings, match details, and club DUPR information.
If you belong to multiple teams, use the My Teams option in the sidebar to select which
team's dashboard and information you want to view.
Mobile Device Usage
The system is fully optimized for desktop computers, tablets, and mobile devices. Please
note that most of the screenshots and instructions in this guide are based on the desktop
version. Layouts, menus, and navigation will automatically adapt to your screen size, so
display and functionality may differ slightly when using a mobile device.
Understanding DUPR Ratings
Season DUPR ratings are displayed throughout the system. To learn how DUPR ratings are
calculated, visit this website: https://www.dupr.com/how-it-works. For questions about
how the Club uses DUPR ratings, which rating is used, or other DUPR-related topics, contact
info@lwrpickleballclub.com.

candidates.content:
6. LEAGUES
6.1. Weekday DUPR League
The Weekday DUPR League is designed for players who have the flexibility to play during
the week and want a structured, team-based competitive experience. Men's and women's
divisions compete separately, with matches typically held at noon during the week. Teams
represent their home communities and travel throughout the Lakewood Ranch area to
compete against other community teams in a round-robin match format. Divisions are
organized using DUPR team rating ranges to promote balanced competition while providing
players with regular opportunities to improve their skills, build friendships, and enjoy the
excitement of representing their community.

candidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
candidates.content:
6.3. PrimeTime DUPR League
The PrimeTime DUPR League is exclusively for players age 65 and older who want
competitive play against others in the same age group. Using DUPR's 65+ age-based rating
system, the league provides a more level playing field by matching players of similar age and
ability. Separate men's and women's divisions compete weekly with two doubles teams
representing each squad, and any tied team match is decided by the exciting Picklebreaker
format. PrimeTime emphasizes spirited competition, sportsmanship, and the opportunity
for experienced players to continue enjoying high-quality league play in a community-
focused environment.

5.5. Roster Requirements & Retroactive Additions: All active players must appear on the
team’s roster in the LMS prior to match play. Retroactive additions are permitted without
penalty only if the player is a valid LWR PC member with an eligible DUPR account and
rating. Failure to meet these requirements will result in a match forfeit, and the match will
not be posted to DUPR.
5.6. DUPR Submission & Eligibility: All qualifying games will be automatically entered into
the DUPR rating system. Games that are forfeited, incomplete, or deemed ineligible will
not be recorded in DUPR (unless otherwise specified by a rule). Individuals/Players are
not authorized to independently submit any Club League scheduled games to DUPR.
5.7. Incomplete Matches: Forfeits vs. Retirements: If a player cannot complete a match for
any reason, the scoring and DUPR eligibility depend on the current score:
5.7.1. Under 6 Points (Forfeit): If neither team has reached 6 points, the match is a
Forfeit, recorded as 0-0, and excluded from DUPR.
5.7.2. 6+ Points (Retired): If at least one team has 6 or more points, the match is recorded
as Retired. Current scores are entered, and results will be posted to DUPR.
5.7.3. Note: In both scenarios, the opposing team is credited with the win. A substitute
may fill in for any remaining games in the session; however, any games left unplayed
without a substitute will be marked as forfeited.
5.8. Coaching & Court Access: Coaching is permitted only during timeouts or between
games. Coaches and non-players must always remain oƯ the court; only active players
may be on the courts.

3.4. Players are assigned to a community based on their primary address at the start of the
season.
3.5. Players may form teams with members from other communities; however, they are not
permitted to play for another community’s team if their own community already has a
team in their division.
3.6. Captains are expected to prioritize players from the local community ahead of those from
outside the community. As a community-based league, we emphasize the inclusion of
local players over non-local players.
3.7. Players are permitted to join or substitute for multiple community teams within the same
community, provided that all League and DUPR rating regulations are adhered to.
3.8. Players must be at least 19 years old.
3.9. Players are responsible for verifying their paddle is on the current Approved Paddle List

upcoming schedules and recent results.

4.1. Season DUPR Ratings: A player's Season DUPR Rating is established on the date
communicated to all captains prior to the first scheduled league match and remains in
eƯect for the duration of the season.
4.1.1. A player with a DUPR Reliability Factor below 29 will be classified as “Not Rated”
(NR) for League purposes and will be subject to the provisions of Rule 4.5. This
classification recognizes that a player’s current DUPR rating may not yet provide a
suƯiciently reliable indication of skill level, particularly for newer or less-established
players or those who have not recently recorded matches in DUPR. Players
classified as “NR” may be placed on a team in the division that most appropriately
reflects their current skill level while they record additional matches and establish a
more reliable DUPR rating. These players are strongly encouraged to consult with a
local Certified DUPR Coach, pickleball professional, or knowledgeable team
captain for guidance regarding appropriate division placement.
4.2. All DUPR ratings will be truncated to the nearest tenth to establish a player's “Season's
DUPR Rating”. For example, a rating of 3.496 will be truncated to 3.4, as will a rating of
3.401.
4.3. Some of our Leagues use the “Age-based” DUPR sub-rating but will still follow all DUPR
Rating/Division Rules. If a player hasn’t established their 65+ Age-based rating as of the
start of a season, their 50+ Age-based rating will be used.
4.4. Any player or team that is found to be cheating, tanking, game-fixing or any kind of data
manipulation, including intentionally creating multiple DUPR accounts, will be banned
from the League for one calendar year.

Match Setup Process
Captains must assign player pairings and save their lineups before the match date. To
ensure fair play, the system automatically checks entries against division ranges, team
totals, and Season DUPR ratings, displaying an on-screen warning if a combination is
ineligible. It is highly recommended that the Home Team enter their lineup first. Lineups
can be changed prior to match day with all changes automatically emailed to opposing
captains.
• In Match Setup, roster choices are filtered against the division’s configured rating
type: Season DUPR, or Age-based/PrimeTime (season_primetime_rating). Players
with no valid rating or outside the division minimum/maximum cannot be selected.
It also checks the two-player combined rating cap.
• Before saving, it refreshes the season ratings and validates again. The save API
repeats that validation server-side, including roster membership, individual rating
range, duplicates, and team-rating maximum.
The rating source is selected by the division’s rating_type: standard divisions use Season
DUPR; PrimeTime/Age-based divisions use the Season PrimeTime rating.
The Match Setup button will show as red if your setup is incomplete, and blue once it is
completed. When both teams have completed their setup, the Match Score Sheet button
will turn green, allowing you to print a complete match score sheet.
Saving a lineup (press the Save Match Setup button) automatically notifies the opposing
captain of the update. From this screen, you can also use the Email Players button to notify
all selected players or the entire team.
For any questions regarding player ratings or eligibility, contact
info@lwrpickleballclub.com.

Quick Start Guide
As a player, you can use the League Management System to view your team schedules,
standings, match details, and club DUPR information.
If you belong to multiple teams, use the My Teams option in the sidebar to select which
team's dashboard and information you want to view.
Mobile Device Usage
The system is fully optimized for desktop computers, tablets, and mobile devices. Please
note that most of the screenshots and instructions in this guide are based on the desktop
version. Layouts, menus, and navigation will automatically adapt to your screen size, so
display and functionality may differ slightly when using a mobile device.
Understanding DUPR Ratings
Season DUPR ratings are displayed throughout the system. To learn how DUPR ratings are
calculated, visit this website: https://www.dupr.com/how-it-works. For questions about
how the Club uses DUPR ratings, which rating is used, or other DUPR-related topics, contact
info@lwrpickleballclub.com.

authorityReviewCandidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR Captains Guide
authorityReviewCandidates.heading: CREATE/UPDATE TEAM ROSTER
authorityReviewCandidates.content:
CREATE/UPDATE TEAM ROSTER
o Enter or update your player team roster prior to the commencement of each season. Use the
Manage Roster option to add or remove players.
 All players must be active Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club members before playing. To
join, they can visit: https://lwrpickleballclub.com/signup.
 All DUPR League players must have a free DUPR ID which can be created at
https://www.dupr.com.
 All players must join the Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club DUPR club (free and
separate from the LWR PC membership) so we can accurately sync player ratings.
Captains should share this link with all players: https://tinyurl.com/LWRPC-DUPRCLUB.
o Roster Requirements & Substitutes: Teams must roster enough players and substitutes (who
are not already on another team) to field a full lineup weekly. For example, if your match
requires 6 players, an 8–10 player roster is recommended. Additional substitutes may be drawn
from other teams in the same community, provided they meet the DUPR division rating
requirements. For complete details, see the Player Requirements and DUPR Rating/Divisions
sections in the DUPR League Mission and Rules.
o Captain Roster Control: Captains are responsible for building their own rosters and may add
or delete players throughout the season as needed provided the player is a current, valid
member of the LWR PC, has a DUPR ID and is eligible for that division.
o Player DUPR Ratings: Season DUPR ratings are updated in the LMS before the season starts
and remain visible to captains all season. For players added midseason, their rating is based on
the date the league's season ratings were originally recorded.

DUPR LEAGUE MANAGERS
Team captains should first attempt to resolve disputes directly, relying on common sense and
fair play. If they cannot reach an agreement, or if further issues arise during the season, DUPR
League Managers will review the matter. All decisions by DUPR League Managers are final and
cannot be appealed.
For questions or concerns, please reach out to one of the following DUPR League Managers:
• Terry Adelman – DUPR League Co-Chair > terry@lwrpickleballclub.com
• Bill Weihs – DUPR League Co-Chair > bill@lwrpickleballclub.com

DUPR LEAGUE RULES
• The DUPR League Mission and League Rules contain the official policies and requirements for
team creation, player eligibility, roster requirements, and specific rules for each of our leagues.
You can access the most current version of this document at any time by logging into the LMS and
selecting League Documents → League Rules from the sidebar menu. The direct link to the current

Quick Start Guide
As a player, you can use the League Management System to view your team schedules,
standings, match details, and club DUPR information.
If you belong to multiple teams, use the My Teams option in the sidebar to select which
team's dashboard and information you want to view.
Mobile Device Usage
The system is fully optimized for desktop computers, tablets, and mobile devices. Please
note that most of the screenshots and instructions in this guide are based on the desktop
version. Layouts, menus, and navigation will automatically adapt to your screen size, so
display and functionality may differ slightly when using a mobile device.
Understanding DUPR Ratings
Season DUPR ratings are displayed throughout the system. To learn how DUPR ratings are
calculated, visit this website: https://www.dupr.com/how-it-works. For questions about
how the Club uses DUPR ratings, which rating is used, or other DUPR-related topics, contact
info@lwrpickleballclub.com.

candidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
candidates.heading: LEAGUES
candidates.content:
6. LEAGUES
6.1. Weekday DUPR League
The Weekday DUPR League is designed for players who have the flexibility to play during
the week and want a structured, team-based competitive experience. Men's and women's
divisions compete separately, with matches typically held at noon during the week. Teams
represent their home communities and travel throughout the Lakewood Ranch area to
compete against other community teams in a round-robin match format. Divisions are
organized using DUPR team rating ranges to promote balanced competition while providing
players with regular opportunities to improve their skills, build friendships, and enjoy the
excitement of representing their community.

candidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
candidates.heading: TEAM/GAME RULES
candidates.content:

discretion of League Management.
5.5. Roster Requirements & Retroactive Additions: All active players must appear on the
team’s roster in the LMS prior to match play. Retroactive additions are permitted without
penalty only if the player is a valid LWR PC member with an eligible DUPR account and
rating. Failure to meet these requirements will result in a match forfeit, and the match will
not be posted to DUPR.
5.6. DUPR Submission & Eligibility: All qualifying games will be automatically entered into
the DUPR rating system. Games that are forfeited, incomplete, or deemed ineligible will
not be recorded in DUPR (unless otherwise specified by a rule). Individuals/Players are
not authorized to independently submit any Club League scheduled games to DUPR.
5.7. Incomplete Matches: Forfeits vs. Retirements: If a player cannot complete a match for
any reason, the scoring and DUPR eligibility depend on the current score:
5.7.1. Under 6 Points (Forfeit): If neither team has reached 6 points, the match is a
Forfeit, recorded as 0-0, and excluded from DUPR.
5.7.2. 6+ Points (Retired): If at least one team has 6 or more points, the match is recorded
as Retired. Current scores are entered, and results will be posted to DUPR.
5.7.3. Note: In both scenarios, the opposing team is credited with the win. A substitute
may fill in for any remaining games in the session; however, any games left unplayed
without a substitute will be marked as forfeited.
5.8. Coaching & Court Access: Coaching is permitted only during timeouts or between
games. Coaches and non-players must always remain oƯ the court; only active players
may be on the courts.

candidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR Captains Guide
candidates.heading: CREATE/UPDATE TEAM ROSTER
candidates.content:
CREATE/UPDATE TEAM ROSTER
o Enter or update your player team roster prior to the commencement of each season. Use the
Manage Roster option to add or remove players.
 All players must be active Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club members before playing. To
join, they can visit: https://lwrpickleballclub.com/signup.
 All DUPR League players must have a free DUPR ID which can be created at
https://www.dupr.com.
 All players must join the Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club DUPR club (free and
separate from the LWR PC membership) so we can accurately sync player ratings.
Captains should share this link with all players: https://tinyurl.com/LWRPC-DUPRCLUB.
o Roster Requirements & Substitutes: Teams must roster enough players and substitutes (who
are not already on another team) to field a full lineup weekly. For example, if your match
requires 6 players, an 8–10 player roster is recommended. Additional substitutes may be drawn
from other teams in the same community, provided they meet the DUPR division rating
requirements. For complete details, see the Player Requirements and DUPR Rating/Divisions
sections in the DUPR League Mission and Rules.
o Captain Roster Control: Captains are responsible for building their own rosters and may add
or delete players throughout the season as needed provided the player is a current, valid
member of the LWR PC, has a DUPR ID and is eligible for that division.
o Player DUPR Ratings: Season DUPR ratings are updated in the LMS before the season starts
and remain visible to captains all season. For players added midseason, their rating is based on
the date the league's season ratings were originally recorded.

candidates.content:
6.3. PrimeTime DUPR League
The PrimeTime DUPR League is exclusively for players age 65 and older who want
competitive play against others in the same age group. Using DUPR's 65+ age-based rating
system, the league provides a more level playing field by matching players of similar age and
ability. Separate men's and women's divisions compete weekly with two doubles teams
representing each squad, and any tied team match is decided by the exciting Picklebreaker
format. PrimeTime emphasizes spirited competition, sportsmanship, and the opportunity
for experienced players to continue enjoying high-quality league play in a community-
focused environment.

candidates.heading: DUPR LEAGUE MANAGERS
candidates.content:
DUPR LEAGUE MANAGERS
Team captains should first attempt to resolve disputes directly, relying on common sense and
fair play. If they cannot reach an agreement, or if further issues arise during the season, DUPR
League Managers will review the matter. All decisions by DUPR League Managers are final and
cannot be appealed.
For questions or concerns, please reach out to one of the following DUPR League Managers:
• Terry Adelman – DUPR League Co-Chair > terry@lwrpickleballclub.com
• Bill Weihs – DUPR League Co-Chair > bill@lwrpickleballclub.com

candidates.heading: Saturday DUPR League Match Day Format
candidates.content:
Saturday DUPR League Match Day Format
The schedule uses two courts for men’s teams and two courts for women’s teams. After the first four
gender-doubles rounds, Men’s Team 3 and Women’s Team 6 play while Mixed Teams 7 and 8 begin.
Round 6 includes the remaining mixed teams. If the match is tied 12-12 after all gender and mixed
doubles, the Picklebreaker is played on two courts using the same mixed teams in the captains’
designated order.

candidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
candidates.content:
6.2. Saturday DUPR League
The Saturday DUPR League is designed for players who prefer weekend competition or are
unable to participate during the week. This coed league features community-based teams
made up of both men and women, competing every other Saturday in a unique format that
includes men's doubles, women's doubles, mixed doubles and the exciting mixed doubles
Picklebreaker to determine tied matches. Teams are grouped into divisions based on
combined DUPR ratings, creating competitive and enjoyable matches while fostering
camaraderie and community spirit throughout the Lakewood Ranch area.

candidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
candidates.heading: PLAYER REQUIREMENTS
candidates.content:
3. PLAYER REQUIREMENTS
3.1. All League players must have a signed/accepted waiver with LWR PC and have a valid
LWR PC membership. To sign up, go to https://lwrpickleballclub.com/signup/.
3.2. All DUPR League players must have a free DUPR ID which can be found at:
https://www.dupr.com/.
3.3. All DUPR League players must join our free DUPR club, which is diƯerent/separate from
the LWR PC membership: https://tinyurl.com/LWRPC-DUPRCLUB
3.4. Players are assigned to a community based on their primary address at the start of the
season.
3.5. Players may form teams with members from other communities; however, they are not
permitted to play for another community’s team if their own community already has a
team in their division.
3.6. Captains are expected to prioritize players from the local community ahead of those from
outside the community. As a community-based league, we emphasize the inclusion of
local players over non-local players.
3.7. Players are permitted to join or substitute for multiple community teams within the same
community, provided that all League and DUPR rating regulations are adhered to.
3.8. Players must be at least 19 years old.
3.9. Players are responsible for verifying their paddle is on the current Approved Paddle List
(https://equipment.usapickleball.org/paddle-list/).

candidates.heading: ALL-STAR TOURNAMENT
candidates.content:
ALL-STAR TOURNAMENT
o The League will hold an All-Star Tournament between seasons. This will be communicated to
all captains prior to Fall/Winter or Winter/Spring season break.
o Each team that participated in the previous season may nominate two players for the All-Star
Tournament. Participation in this tournament is optional, and teams are not obligated to
compete.
o All regular season eligibility standards, ratings and rules apply and will be based on the previous
season.
o These games will not be posted to DUPR.
o A double-elimination tournament will determine the All-Star Champs for each Division.
o The League will award medals to Gold/1st place winners in each Division.

suppliedEvidence.heading: DUPR RATINGS/DIVISIONS
suppliedEvidence.content:
4. DUPR RATINGS/DIVISIONS
4.1. Season DUPR Ratings: A player's Season DUPR Rating is established on the date
communicated to all captains prior to the first scheduled league match and remains in
eƯect for the duration of the season.
4.1.1. A player with a DUPR Reliability Factor below 29 will be classified as “Not Rated”
(NR) for League purposes and will be subject to the provisions of Rule 4.5. This
classification recognizes that a player’s current DUPR rating may not yet provide a
suƯiciently reliable indication of skill level, particularly for newer or less-established
players or those who have not recently recorded matches in DUPR. Players
classified as “NR” may be placed on a team in the division that most appropriately
reflects their current skill level while they record additional matches and establish a
more reliable DUPR rating. These players are strongly encouraged to consult with a
local Certified DUPR Coach, pickleball professional, or knowledgeable team
captain for guidance regarding appropriate division placement.
4.2. All DUPR ratings will be truncated to the nearest tenth to establish a player's “Season's
DUPR Rating”. For example, a rating of 3.496 will be truncated to 3.4, as will a rating of
3.401.
4.3. Some of our Leagues use the “Age-based” DUPR sub-rating but will still follow all DUPR
Rating/Division Rules. If a player hasn’t established their 65+ Age-based rating as of the
start of a season, their 50+ Age-based rating will be used.
4.4. Any player or team that is found to be cheating, tanking, game-fixing or any kind of data
manipulation, including intentionally creating multiple DUPR accounts, will be banned
from the League for one calendar year.

suppliedEvidence.heading: Team DUPR Rating Requirements
suppliedEvidence.content:
4.6. Team DUPR Rating Requirements: A team's DUPR Rating is calculated by adding the
Season DUPR Ratings of both players. Each division has established minimum and
maximum individual player ratings, as well as a maximum combined Team DUPR
Rating. These limits are strictly enforced.
4.6.1. Every lineup fielded for a match must comply with both the individual player rating
requirements and the maximum combined Team DUPR Rating for that division.
Teams that fail to meet these requirements will automatically forfeit the aƯected
games.
4.6.2. Games forfeited due to an invalid lineup will not be submitted to DUPR. The
League Management System will automatically record the forfeits and update team
records and league standings accordingly.

competingEvidence.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
competingEvidence.heading: DUPR RATINGS/DIVISIONS
competingEvidence.content:
4. DUPR RATINGS/DIVISIONS
4.1. Season DUPR Ratings: A player's Season DUPR Rating is established on the date
communicated to all captains prior to the first scheduled league match and remains in
eƯect for the duration of the season.
4.1.1. A player with a DUPR Reliability Factor below 29 will be classified as “Not Rated”
(NR) for League purposes and will be subject to the provisions of Rule 4.5. This
classification recognizes that a player’s current DUPR rating may not yet provide a
suƯiciently reliable indication of skill level, particularly for newer or less-established
players or those who have not recently recorded matches in DUPR. Players
classified as “NR” may be placed on a team in the division that most appropriately
reflects their current skill level while they record additional matches and establish a
more reliable DUPR rating. These players are strongly encouraged to consult with a
local Certified DUPR Coach, pickleball professional, or knowledgeable team
captain for guidance regarding appropriate division placement.
4.2. All DUPR ratings will be truncated to the nearest tenth to establish a player's “Season's
DUPR Rating”. For example, a rating of 3.496 will be truncated to 3.4, as will a rating of
3.401.
4.3. Some of our Leagues use the “Age-based” DUPR sub-rating but will still follow all DUPR
Rating/Division Rules. If a player hasn’t established their 65+ Age-based rating as of the
start of a season, their 50+ Age-based rating will be used.
4.4. Any player or team that is found to be cheating, tanking, game-fixing or any kind of data
manipulation, including intentionally creating multiple DUPR accounts, will be banned
from the League for one calendar year.
4.5. Players with a DUPR Rating of "NR" (Not Rated): Players with a DUPR rating of NR (Not

competingEvidence.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
competingEvidence.heading: Team DUPR Rating Requirements
competingEvidence.content:
4.6. Team DUPR Rating Requirements: A team's DUPR Rating is calculated by adding the
Season DUPR Ratings of both players. Each division has established minimum and
maximum individual player ratings, as well as a maximum combined Team DUPR
Rating. These limits are strictly enforced.
4.6.1. Every lineup fielded for a match must comply with both the individual player rating
requirements and the maximum combined Team DUPR Rating for that division.
Teams that fail to meet these requirements will automatically forfeit the aƯected
games.
4.6.2. Games forfeited due to an invalid lineup will not be submitted to DUPR. The
League Management System will automatically record the forfeits and update team
records and league standings accordingly.

a Certified DUPR Coach or qualified pickleball professional provide input to help
determine the player's most appropriate skill level. The team captain is ultimately
responsible for ensuring the player is placed in the proper division to promote balanced
and fair competition for all teams.
4.5.1. For team aggregate rating calculations, an NR player will initially be assigned a
Season DUPR Rating equal to the maximum individual DUPR rating allowed for
that division, minus 0.5. For example, in a division, where the maximum individual
rating is 3.8, an NR player would be assigned an initial Season DUPR Rating of 3.3
(3.8 − 0.5) for team aggregate calculations.
4.5.2. If a player is rostered on teams in multiple divisions, the highest adjusted Season
DUPR Rating assigned to that player will be used consistently across all divisions in
which they appear.

5.5. Roster Requirements & Retroactive Additions: All active players must appear on the
team’s roster in the LMS prior to match play. Retroactive additions are permitted without
penalty only if the player is a valid LWR PC member with an eligible DUPR account and
rating. Failure to meet these requirements will result in a match forfeit, and the match will
not be posted to DUPR.
5.6. DUPR Submission & Eligibility: All qualifying games will be automatically entered into
the DUPR rating system. Games that are forfeited, incomplete, or deemed ineligible will
not be recorded in DUPR (unless otherwise specified by a rule). Individuals/Players are
not authorized to independently submit any Club League scheduled games to DUPR.
5.7. Incomplete Matches: Forfeits vs. Retirements: If a player cannot complete a match for
any reason, the scoring and DUPR eligibility depend on the current score:
5.7.1. Under 6 Points (Forfeit): If neither team has reached 6 points, the match is a
Forfeit, recorded as 0-0, and excluded from DUPR.
5.7.2. 6+ Points (Retired): If at least one team has 6 or more points, the match is recorded
as Retired. Current scores are entered, and results will be posted to DUPR.
5.7.3. Note: In both scenarios, the opposing team is credited with the win. A substitute
may fill in for any remaining games in the session; however, any games left unplayed
without a substitute will be marked as forfeited.
5.8. Coaching & Court Access: Coaching is permitted only during timeouts or between
games. Coaches and non-players must always remain oƯ the court; only active players
may be on the courts.

the rally.

candidates.heading: 21.C Medical Time-Out — Between Games
candidates.content:

medical time-out, when available, before the start of the next
game.

candidates.heading: 21.C Medical Time-Out — Valid Medical Condition
candidates.content:
21.C.8 Valid Medical Condition. When medical personnel, or the
Tournament Director, when medical personnel are not available,
determine that a valid medical condition exists, the player must
be able to resume play in 15 minutes or less. When the player is
able to resume play in fewer than 15 minutes, the remaining
medical time is lost and no longer available to the player during
the match.

candidates.heading: 21.D Referee Time-Out — Resuming Play
candidates.content:
21.D.4 Resuming Play. The referee will resume play by announcing a
15-second warning (Rule 17.D.16).

candidates.heading: 21.F Time-Out Between Games — Resuming Play
candidates.content:

candidates.heading: 21.B End Change Time-Out — Resuming Play
candidates.content:
21.B.8 Resuming Play. The referee will resume play by announcing a
15-second warning (Rule 17.D.16).

candidates.heading: 21.C Medical Time-Out — Time Start
candidates.content:
21.C.7 Time Start. When medical assistance arrives, the referee will
start a 15-minute timer. Play must resume as soon as possible
but no later than 15 minutes of elapsed time.

candidates.heading: 21.D Referee Time-Out — Referee Discretion
candidates.content:
21.D.1 Referee Discretion. In the interest of overall safety, when the
referee determines a potential medical situation exists, the
referee is authorized to call a referee time-out and summon
medical personnel, or the Tournament Director when medical
personnel are not available.

candidates.heading: 21.C Medical Time-Out — Summoning Medical Assistance
candidates.content:
21.C.5 Summoning Medical Assistance. The referee will immediately
summon on-site medical personnel to assess the situation and
render appropriate first aid. When medical personnel are not
available, the Tournament Director will be summoned for
assistance.

candidates.heading: Suspended Game
candidates.content:
21.H Suspended Game. A game suspended due to extenuating circumstances
must resume with the same server, score, and remaining time-outs as when
the game was suspended.

candidates.heading: 21.B End Change Time-Out — Duration
candidates.content:
21.B.5 Duration. A maximum of one minute is allowed to change ends
during a game.

candidates.heading: Damaged Ball
candidates.content:
10.G Damaged Ball. When a ball is or becomes broken, cracked, soft or degraded,
play must continue until the end of the rally. The ball will be replaced if all
players agree.

candidates.heading: Medical Time-Out
candidates.content:
21.C Medical Time-Out. A player needing medical attention during a match,
including between games, may request a medical time-out.

candidates.heading: Player Equipment or Apparel Problem
candidates.content:
10.I Player Equipment or Apparel Problem. If a player experiences an
equipment or apparel problem during a rally, play must continue until the
end of the rally.

candidates.heading: 21.F Time-Out Between Games — Duration
candidates.content:
21.F.1 Duration. A maximum of two minutes is allowed to change ends
between games.

candidates.heading: 21.D Referee Time-Out — Presence of Blood
candidates.content:
21.D.2 Presence of Blood. When a player is actively bleeding or blood
is found on the court or a player, play must be stopped at the
end of the rally. Play must not resume until the blood has been
cleaned up and the bleeding has been controlled. Issues relating
solely to blood cleanup or control that do not require the
services of medical personnel will be addressed as a referee
time-out.

candidates.heading: Roster Continuity
candidates.content:
5.13.3. Roster Continuity: When a game is rescheduled, the players originally assigned to
it must participate and maintain their original positions/line assignments.
5.14. End of Season PlayoƯs/Championship Day (All Leagues)
5.14.1. Teams starting the season with fewer scheduled games than others in their
Division/Pool will receive compensatory points at the end of the season. These
points will be calculated based on the team’s average points earned per match
date, rounded to the nearest whole number (0.5 and above rounds up; 0.4 and
below rounds down).

candidates.heading: 21.C Medical Time-Out — Technical Warning or Technical Foul – Invalid Medical
candidates.content:
21.C.10 Technical Warning or Technical Foul – Invalid Medical
Condition. When medical personnel, or the Tournament
Director when medical personnel are not available, determine
that no valid medical condition exists for granting a medical
timeout, the referee will assess a technical warning and charge
a standard time-out against the singles player or doubles team
that requested the medical time-out. When a standard time-
out is not available, the referee will assess a technical foul
against the player or team. The medical time-out is no longer
available to that player and the player must resume play
immediately.

candidates.heading: 21.C Medical Time-Out — Before Start of Match
candidates.content:
21.C.1 Before Start of Match. A medical time-out cannot be called
before the start of a match.

candidates.documentTitle: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules
candidates.heading: Weather Issues
candidates.content:
6.2.7. Weather Issues: If games are aƯected by weather-related issues and both teams
are unable to reschedule them within the permitted league timeframe, the
matches will officially be scored as a “weather related” resulting in a 13-13 tie.
6.2.8. Snacks/Drinks: Optional; the Home Team may provide them if desired.
6.2.9. Jamboree: held at the end of the season.

candidates.heading: 22.I Match Forfeit by Referee — Late Reporting for Multiple-Game Match
candidates.content: 22.I.4 Late Reporting for Multiple-Game Match. See Rule 18.F.2.

candidates.heading: Player Repositioning
candidates.content:
20.D Player Repositioning. After the score is called, when the serving team
changes serving areas, the referee must stop play, allow all players to
reposition, and re-call the score to restart the 10-second count. (Modifies
Rule 6.D.2)

candidates.heading: 21.C Medical Time-Out — Number Available
candidates.content:
21.C.3 Number Available. A player may be granted only one medical
time-out per match.

candidates.heading: 21.B End Change Time-Out — Failure to Change Ends
candidates.content:
21.B.7 Failure to Change Ends. When an end change is not executed at
the required point score, the end change will be executed when
the failure to change ends is detected. It is not a fault on either
team, the score is not impacted, and service continues with the
same server.

candidates.heading: 21.C Medical Time-Out — Duration
candidates.content:
21.C.6 Duration. A maximum of 15 minutes is allowed for a medical
time-out. However, when medical treatment is rendered off-
court at another location at the venue, the time to transport the
player to and from the off-court location will be excluded from
15-minute time period.

candidates.heading: End Change Time-Out
candidates.content:
21.B End Change Time-Out. The referee will call a time-out to allow players to
change ends at specified points during single-game matches and tie-
breaker games. Players will not change ends during the tie-breaker game
when the first game of the match was forfeited due to late arrival.
21.B.1 11-Point Game. In a single game or tie-breaker game to 11
points, the players will change ends when the first singles player
or doubles team reaches a score of 6.
21.B.2 15-Point Game. In a single game or tie-breaker game to 15
points, the players will change ends when the first singles player
or doubles team reaches a score of 8.
21.B.3 21-Point Game. In a single game or tie-breaker game to 21
points, the players will change ends when the first singles player
or doubles team reaches a score of 11.

candidates.heading: 22.I Match Forfeit by Referee — Late Reporting for First Game
candidates.content: 22.I.3 Late Reporting for First Game. See Rule 18.F.1.

candidates.heading: Damaged Ball
candidates.content:
10.G Damaged Ball. When a ball is or becomes broken, cracked, soft or degraded,
play must continue until the end of the rally. The ball will be replaced if all
players agree.

candidates.heading: 17.D Officiating Play — Damaged Balls
candidates.content:
17.D.14 Damaged Balls. Determine whether a ball is broken or cracked
and must be replaced, and whether the broken or cracked ball
affected the outcome of a rally. (See Rule 20.F.)

candidates.heading: Damaged Ball
candidates.content:
20.F Damaged Ball. A player may appeal to the referee to determine whether a
ball is degraded, soft, broken, or cracked. A potentially soft or degraded
ball will not be replaced unless all players agree. If the referee determines
that the ball is broken or cracked, it will be replaced. (Modifies Rule 10.G)

candidates.heading: 20.F Damaged Ball — Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball
candidates.content:
20.F.1 Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball. When the referee determines
that the broken or cracked ball affected the outcome of the rally,
the rally must be replayed with a replacement ball. (Modifies
Rule 10.G.1)

candidates.heading: 10.G Damaged Ball — Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball
candidates.content:
10.G.1 Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball. When all players agree that a
broken or cracked ball affected the outcome of the rally, the rally
must be replayed. If all players do not agree that a broken or
cracked ball affected the outcome of the rally, the result of the rally
stands.

candidates.heading: 25.C Hybrid Doubles Play — Adaptive Standing Players
candidates.content:
25.C.3 Adaptive Standing Players. Eligible adaptive standing players
(per Rule 25.B.3.a) are the only standing players who may use
the two-bounce allowance in hybrid play and must declare this
accommodation before the match.
Appendix B Rulebook Priorities and Guiding
Principles
Preface
The USA Pickleball Official Rulebook is the organization’s most important product.
It is the foundational document for the sport of pickleball and should be treated
with the respect accorded the sport’s founders and those who have written and
approved rules over the years.
Writing rules that are objective, clear, and concise is difficult work. Because those
involved in writing and/or approving rules come from diverse backgrounds and
experiences, it is important to have rule writing priorities and guiding principles
that help provide a measure of consistency from year to year. The following
Rulebook Priorities and Guiding Principles were developed to guide rule writers and
approvers in their important work.
Priorities
The following three priorities should be considered “tests” for any suggested rule
change. Any suggested rule change should satisfy at least one of these three
priorities, listed in order of importance:
1. The first priority is preserving the integrity of the sport, one that incorporates
the elements of fun, cooperation, courtesy, and competition. This priority pays
homage to those who developed the sport in 1965 and those who have written
and approved rule changes over the years.
2. The second priority is what is collectively best for the players. This priority
examines rule changes for improving the player’s experience. It “tests”
suggested rule changes from the standpoint of minimizing player
disagreements, making it easier to learn the sport, teach the sport, and play
the sport, while also allowing for moderate innovation as player skills and
equipment develop and evolve.
3. The third priority is what is best for officiating. It “tests” rule changes to make it
less likely conflicts will occur between players as well as between players and
officials.
Guiding Principles
The USA Pickleball Official Rulebook contains a wide variety of rules that cover the
court and equipment, recreational and social play as well as tournament play,
officiated and non-officiated. The following are Guiding Principles for those writing
and approving rules. To the extent possible, rules should:
1. Apply to all levels and categories of players: recreational and social players, as
well as professional and amateur tournament players (officiated and non-
officiated). Specific rules for a single category of player, for example, the pro
level player, should be approved after careful consideration and examination
of how the rule change might impact the sport beyond the pro level of
competition.
2. Be written with a deterministic focus, i.e., from the standpoint of “if this occurs,
this is what happens.” If something is not allowed or should not happen, the
consequences (for example: replay, fault, technical warning, etc.) should be
provided as part of the rule (e.g., replay, fault, technical warning, etc.).
3. Center on that which should not occur, not on what is permitted or allowed.
Attempts to include rules describing what is allowed will result in an
unnecessarily lengthy Rulebook.
4. Avoid ambiguity, player discretion, or referee judgment-related rules. Such
rules invite disagreements and different interpretations. To this end, when a
key word is used to describe when a rule applies, the word should be defined
as either a part of the rule or in the Definition section of the Rulebook.
5. Allow equipment manufacturers to innovate, as long as such innovation does
not overwhelm or outpace the average player’s ability to keep up with the
speed and difficulty of the sport. Equipment-related rule changes should be
given particularly close scrutiny because of their precedent-setting potential.
6. Have an element of precedent accorded to them. Change for change’s sake
should be avoided to avoid frustration among, or a loss of confidence by,
players.
7. Allow for an appropriate degree of player innovation. Such innovation should
maintain a healthy balance between historical rules that have been
instrumental to the sport’s growth and appeal.
8. Preserve the unique features and rules of the sport involving the Non-Volley
Zone and the two-bounce rule and prevent one shot, one paddle, or one type
of play from dominating the sport.
9. Address a known issue or anticipate trends and needs of the sport before
problems develop.
10. Be subjected to reviews and comments by domestic and international
stakeholders.

candidates.heading: 10.C Returned Ball Placement — Fault – Ball Hits Permanent Object After Landing
candidates.content:
10.C.5 Fault – Ball Hits Permanent Object After Landing. When a player
fails to return a ball that has bounced in the player’s court before
the ball contacts a permanent object, it is a fault against that
player.

candidates.heading: 10.C Returned Ball Placement — Fault – Ball Hits Player
candidates.content:
10.C.3 Fault – Ball Hits Player. After the serve, when the ball contacts a
player or anything that is worn or carried by the player, except the
player’s paddle or the player’s hands below the wrist joint while in
contact with the paddle, it is a fault against that player.

candidates.heading: 10.C Returned Ball Placement — Fault – Ball Hits Permanent Object Before Landing
candidates.content:
10.C.4 Fault – Ball Hits Permanent Object Before Landing. When a
player hits a ball that contacts a permanent object before
bouncing on the court, it is a fault against that player.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: 13.I.2 Ball Crosses Back to Opponent’s Side — Fault – Ball Not Contacted
candidates.content:
13.I.2.b Fault – Ball Not Contacted. When a ball bounces in
the court on the receiving player’s end of the net and
then returns to the opponent’s end of the net without
being hit, it is a fault against a player who fails to hit
the ball before it bounces once on the opponent’s end
of the net.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 9: Dead Balls, Faults, and Hinders
candidates.heading: 9.B Faults — Fault Occurrence
candidates.content:
9.B.1 Fault Occurrence. A fault only occurs while the ball is live, except
for non-volley zone violations involving momentum. (See Rule
11.A.2.)

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: 13.E Ball Under Net — Fault – Ball Under Net
candidates.content:
13.E.1 Fault – Ball Under Net. When a player hits the ball under the net, it
is a fault against the player.

candidates.heading: 10.D Double Hit — Fault – Ball Hit by Two-Players
candidates.content:
10.D.2 Fault – Ball Hit by Two-Players. It is a fault if both a player and
their partner strike the ball while attempting to return it.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: 13.I.1 After Hitting the Ball — Fault – Player Crosses Plane of Net Before Hitting
candidates.content:
13.I.1.a Fault – Player Crosses Plane of Net Before Hitting
Ball. When any part of a player or anything that is worn
or carried by the player crosses the plane of the net
before the player hits the ball, it is a fault against the
player.

candidates.heading: 10.G Damaged Ball — No Replay – Soft or Degraded Ball
candidates.content:
10.G.2 No Replay – Soft or Degraded Ball. When a ball is or becomes
degraded or soft, the result of the prior rally stands.

candidates.heading: 10.C Returned Ball Placement — Fault – Ball Lands on Player’s Side of Net
candidates.content:
10.C.2 Fault – Ball Lands on Player’s Side of Net. When a player hits a
ball that fails to cross the net and lands on the player’s side of the
net, it is a fault against that player.

candidates.heading: 10.C Returned Ball Placement — Fault – Ball Lands Out of Bounds
candidates.content:
10.C.1 Fault – Ball Lands Out of Bounds. When a player hits a ball that
first lands outside the opponent’s end of the court, it is a fault
against that player.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: 13.F Ball Crossing Plane of Net — Fault – Ball Hit Before Crossing Plane of Net
candidates.content:
13.F.1 Fault – Ball Hit Before Crossing Plane of Net. When a player hits
the ball before the ball entirely crosses the plane of the net to the
player’s end, it is a fault against the player.

candidates.heading: 25.A.9 Two-Bounce Allowance — Fault – Failure to Return Ball Before Third Bounce.
candidates.content:
25.A.9.a Fault – Failure to Return Ball Before Third Bounce.
When a wheelchair player does not return a ball
before it bounces three times, it is a fault against the
player. (Modifies Rule 10.B.1)

candidates.heading: 25.B.3 Two-Bounce Allowance — Fault – Failure to Return Ball Before Third Bounce.
candidates.content:
25.B.3.c Fault – Failure to Return Ball Before Third Bounce.
When the player does not return a ball before it
bounces three times, it is a fault against the player.
(Modifies Rule 10.B.1.)

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: 13.I.1 After Hitting the Ball — Fault – Player Crosses Plane of Net Without Hitting
candidates.content:
13.I.1.b Fault – Player Crosses Plane of Net Without Hitting
Ball. When any part of a player or anything that is worn
or carried by the player crosses the plane of the net
and the player does not hit the ball, it is a fault against
the player.

candidates.heading: 24.B Extra Ball — Fault – Extra Ball Visible or Ball Falls
candidates.content:
24.B.1 Fault – Extra Ball Visible or Ball Falls. When an extra ball
carried by a player is visible to an opponent or falls to the
playing surface while the ball is live, it is a fault against the
player.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: 13.I.2 Ball Crosses Back to Opponent’s Side — Fault – Player Crosses Plane of Net Before Ball
candidates.content:
13.I.2.a Fault – Player Crosses Plane of Net Before Ball
Crosses. When a ball bounces in the court on the
receiving player’s end of the net and is returning to the
opponent’s end without being hit, it is a fault against
the player if the player crosses the plane of the net
before the ball crosses entirely.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: 13.D Ball Between Net and Net Post — Fault – Ball Between Net and Net Post
candidates.content:
13.D.1 Fault – Ball Between Net and Net Post. When a player hits the
ball between the net and the net post, it is a fault against the
player.

candidates.heading: Returned Ball Placement
candidates.content:
10.C Returned Ball Placement. A player must return the ball so that the ball
lands on the opponent’s end of the court or contacts the opponent or
anything that is worn or carried by the opponent before the ball lands.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 9: Dead Balls, Faults, and Hinders
candidates.heading: Faults
candidates.content: 9.B Faults. A called fault or a fault committed by a player results in a dead ball.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: 13.B Ball Contacting Net Support System — Fault – Ball Contacts Net Support System
candidates.content:
13.B.1 Fault – Ball Contacts Net Support System. When a player serves a
ball that contacts the net support system on either end of the net
or returns a ball that contacts the net support system before going
over the net, it is a fault against the player.

candidates.heading: 22.B Verbal and Technical Warnings — Ball Abuse
candidates.content:
22.B.4 Ball Abuse. Intentionally damaging or aggressively hitting a
dead ball without endangering people.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: 13.B Ball Contacting Net Support System — Replay – Ball Affected by Net Support System
candidates.content:
13.B.2 Replay – Ball Affected by Net Support System. When a returned
ball crosses the net and contacts any part of a crossbar, or any
other part of the net support system within the court boundaries,
before or after the ball bounces, the rally must be replayed.

candidates.heading: 3.C Ball Specifications — Construction
candidates.content:
3.C.5 Construction. The ball must be made of durable material molded
with a smooth surface and free of texturing. The ball may have a
slight ridge at the seam, as long as it does not significantly impact
the ball’s flight characteristics. (See Figure 3-2.)
The ball with larger holes is customarily used
for indoor play (pictured on the left). The ball
with smaller holes is customarily used for
outdoor play (pictured on the right).
Figure 3-2: Approved Balls – Examples

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: Ball Around Net Post
candidates.content:
13.C Ball Around Net Post. A ball may be returned around the outside of the net
post.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: Ball Contacting Net
candidates.content:
13.A Ball Contacting Net. When the ball contacts the net, or the rope or cable at
the top of the net between the net posts, the ball remains in play.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: 13.B Ball Contacting Net Support System — Replay – Ball Affected by Net Support System
candidates.content:
13.B.2 Replay – Ball Affected by Net Support System. When a returned
ball crosses the net and contacts any part of a crossbar, or any
other part of the net support system within the court boundaries,
before or after the ball bounces, the rally must be replayed.

candidates.heading: 25.B.3 Two-Bounce Allowance — Dead Ball
candidates.content:
25.B.3.d Dead Ball. When the ball strikes a permanent object
(e.g., fence, wall) before the second bounce, it is a
dead ball and the rally ends.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: 13.A Ball Contacting Net — Replay – Ball Contacts Net
candidates.content:
13.A.1 Replay – Ball Contacts Net. When a returned ball that crosses the
net gets caught in the net, contacts a part of the net that is draping
on the ground, or contacts a deflecting net before or after
bouncing, the rally must be replayed.

candidates.heading: Player Equipment or Apparel Problem
candidates.content:
10.I Player Equipment or Apparel Problem. If a player experiences an
equipment or apparel problem during a rally, play must continue until the
end of the rally.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 6: Player Readiness and Calling the
candidates.heading: 6.F Challenging the Score Call — Incorrect Score Identified After Rally
candidates.content:
6.F.4 Incorrect Score Identified After Rally. When an incorrect score
was called and the rally is completed, the result of the rally stands,
and the score must be corrected before the next serve.

candidates.heading: 5.C Questions About Correct Server, Receiver, and Positions — Player or Position Error Identified After Rally
candidates.content:
5.C.2 Player or Position Error Identified After Rally. When the correct
server or correct receiver is not in their correct position when the
score is called and the rally is completed, the result of the rally
stands.

candidates.heading: Standard Scoring
candidates.content:
4.A Standard Scoring. A point is scored by serving the ball and winning the
rally. (See Rule 14.A.2 for the rally scoring option.)

candidates.heading: Catch or Carry
candidates.content:
12.C Catch or Carry. A player must not catch or carry a ball on their paddle
during a rally.

candidates.heading: 25.B.2 Assistive Devices — Prohibited Use
candidates.content:
25.B.2.b Prohibited Use. Assistive devices must not be used
to strike the ball or to intentionally alter its flight. If
an assistive device contacts a live ball, the ball
becomes dead and the rally ends.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 6: Player Readiness and Calling the
candidates.heading: Challenging the Score Call
candidates.content:
6.F Challenging the Score Call. A player may stop a rally to ask for a score
correction before the return of serve is hit and before the ball becomes dead.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: 13.I.2 Ball Crosses Back to Opponent’s Side — Fault – Ball Not Contacted
candidates.content:
13.I.2.b Fault – Ball Not Contacted. When a ball bounces in
the court on the receiving player’s end of the net and
then returns to the opponent’s end of the net without
being hit, it is a fault against a player who fails to hit
the ball before it bounces once on the opponent’s end
of the net.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 6: Player Readiness and Calling the
candidates.heading: 6.F Challenging the Score Call — Replay – Incorrect Score Called
candidates.content:
6.F.1 Replay – Incorrect Score Called. When an incorrect score is called
and the rally is stopped before the return of serve and before the
ball becomes dead, the rally must be replayed with the correct
score called.

candidates.heading: 10.C Returned Ball Placement — Fault – Ball Hits Player
candidates.content:
10.C.3 Fault – Ball Hits Player. After the serve, when the ball contacts a
player or anything that is worn or carried by the player, except the
player’s paddle or the player’s hands below the wrist joint while in
contact with the paddle, it is a fault against that player.

candidates.heading: 10.C Returned Ball Placement — Fault – Ball Hits Permanent Object After Landing
candidates.content:
10.C.5 Fault – Ball Hits Permanent Object After Landing. When a player
fails to return a ball that has bounced in the player’s court before
the ball contacts a permanent object, it is a fault against that
player.

candidates.heading: The Game
candidates.content:
bounce can be anywhere on the playing surface.
Underlying Principles
Pickleball is a game that requires cooperation and courtesy. A sense of fair
play by giving the opponent the benefit of any doubt is essential in
maintaining the game’s underlying principles of fun and competition.
• All points played are treated the same regardless of their importance: the
first point of the match is as important as match point.
• Either partner in doubles can make calls, especially line calls.
• Calls are made promptly to preserve fair play and prevent players from
making delayed calls for their own advantage.
• Players strive to cooperate when confronted with a situation not covered
by the Rulebook. Resolutions can be made by asking for a referee to
resolve a dispute. allowing the rally to stand, or in extreme cases, a replay
of the rally.
• Where possible, rules accommodate players with various adaptive needs.
• Players avoid wearing clothing that closely matches the ball color.
• Players should not question or comment on an opponent’s call except
through an appeal to a referee.

candidates.heading: 12.C Catch or Carry — Fault – Catch or Carry
candidates.content:
12.C.1 Fault – Catch or Carry. When a player catches or carries a ball on
their paddle during a rally, it is a fault against the player.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 9: Dead Balls, Faults, and Hinders
candidates.heading: 9.A Stopping a Rally — Fault – Stopping a Rally
candidates.content:
9.A.1 Fault – Stopping a Rally. When a player stops a rally before the
ball otherwise becomes dead, it is a fault against the player unless
the stoppage is to call a hinder (see Rule 9.C), to correctly identify a
player position or server error (see Rule 5.C.1.a), or to ask for
correction of an incorrect score before the return of serve (see Rule
6.F.1).

candidates.heading: 5.B Doubles — Player Positions During Rallies
candidates.content:
5.B.4 Player Positions During Rallies. Except while serving and
receiving, there is no restriction on the position of the players, on
or off the court, as long as they are on their respective end of the
net while the ball is live, except when a player crosses the plane of
the net as allowed in Rule 13.I.

candidates.heading: Extra Ball
candidates.content:
24.B Extra Ball. An extra ball carried by a player during a rally must not be
visible to the opponent and must remain in possession of the player.

candidates.heading: 25.B.3 Two-Bounce Allowance — Fault – Failure to Return Ball Before Third Bounce.
candidates.content:
25.B.3.c Fault – Failure to Return Ball Before Third Bounce.
When the player does not return a ball before it
bounces three times, it is a fault against the player.
(Modifies Rule 10.B.1.)

candidates.heading: Between Rallies
candidates.content:
10.K Between Rallies. Players may quickly hydrate, towel off, and adjust
equipment and apparel between rallies as long as the flow of the game is not
adversely impacted.

candidates.heading: 5.C.1 Player or Position Error Claimed During Rally — Replay – Correct Claim
candidates.content:
5.C.1.a Replay – Correct Claim. If the correct server or correct
receiver is not in their correct position when the score
is called and a player stops the rally to correctly
identify the player or position error, the rally must be
replayed.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 9: Dead Balls, Faults, and Hinders
candidates.heading: 9.B Faults — Fault Occurrence
candidates.content:
9.B.1 Fault Occurrence. A fault only occurs while the ball is live, except
for non-volley zone violations involving momentum. (See Rule
11.A.2.)

candidates.heading: 20.E.2 Replays — Replay – Drop Serve, Questionable Force on Ball.
candidates.content:
20.E.2.i Replay – Drop Serve, Questionable Force on Ball.
When it is questionable whether the ball was
propelled when the server released the ball to make
a drop serve, the referee must call for a replay.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: 13.I Player Crossing Plane of Net — Ball Crosses Back to Opponent’s Side
candidates.content:
13.I.2 Ball Crosses Back to Opponent’s Side. When a ball bounces in the
court on the receiving player’s end of the net and then returns to
the opponent’s side of the net without being hit, the receiving
player may cross over, under, or around the net to hit the ball, but
only after the ball has first crossed back to the opponent’s end of
the net.

playing surface while the ball is live, it is a fault against the
player.

the ball before the ball entirely crosses the plane of the net to the
player’s end, it is a fault against the player.

dead ball without endangering people.

player hits a ball that contacts a permanent object before
bouncing on the court, it is a fault against that player.

candidates.content:

releasing the ball to make the serve.

against that player.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: 13.I.1 After Hitting the Ball — Fault – Player Crosses Plane of Net Before Hitting
candidates.content:
13.I.1.a Fault – Player Crosses Plane of Net Before Hitting
Ball. When any part of a player or anything that is worn
or carried by the player crosses the plane of the net
before the player hits the ball, it is a fault against the
player.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: 13.I.1 After Hitting the Ball — Fault – Player Crosses Plane of Net Without Hitting
candidates.content:
13.I.1.b Fault – Player Crosses Plane of Net Without Hitting
Ball. When any part of a player or anything that is worn
or carried by the player crosses the plane of the net
and the player does not hit the ball, it is a fault against
the player.

candidates.heading: The Game
candidates.content:
bounce can be anywhere on the playing surface.
Underlying Principles
Pickleball is a game that requires cooperation and courtesy. A sense of fair
play by giving the opponent the benefit of any doubt is essential in
maintaining the game’s underlying principles of fun and competition.
• All points played are treated the same regardless of their importance: the
first point of the match is as important as match point.
• Either partner in doubles can make calls, especially line calls.
• Calls are made promptly to preserve fair play and prevent players from
making delayed calls for their own advantage.
• Players strive to cooperate when confronted with a situation not covered
by the Rulebook. Resolutions can be made by asking for a referee to
resolve a dispute. allowing the rally to stand, or in extreme cases, a replay
of the rally.
• Where possible, rules accommodate players with various adaptive needs.
• Players avoid wearing clothing that closely matches the ball color.
• Players should not question or comment on an opponent’s call except
through an appeal to a referee.

candidates.heading: 10.C Returned Ball Placement — Fault – Ball Lands on Player’s Side of Net
candidates.content:
10.C.2 Fault – Ball Lands on Player’s Side of Net. When a player hits a
ball that fails to cross the net and lands on the player’s side of the
net, it is a fault against that player.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: Ball Contacting Net Support System
candidates.content:
13.B Ball Contacting Net Support System. A served ball must not contact any
part of the net support system. A returned ball must not contact any part of
the net support system on the hitting player’s end of the net.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: 13.D Ball Between Net and Net Post — Fault – Ball Between Net and Net Post
candidates.content:
13.D.1 Fault – Ball Between Net and Net Post. When a player hits the
ball between the net and the net post, it is a fault against the
player.

candidates.heading: End Change Time-Out
candidates.content:
21.B End Change Time-Out. The referee will call a time-out to allow players to
change ends at specified points during single-game matches and tie-
breaker games. Players will not change ends during the tie-breaker game
when the first game of the match was forfeited due to late arrival.
21.B.1 11-Point Game. In a single game or tie-breaker game to 11
points, the players will change ends when the first singles player
or doubles team reaches a score of 6.
21.B.2 15-Point Game. In a single game or tie-breaker game to 15
points, the players will change ends when the first singles player
or doubles team reaches a score of 8.
21.B.3 21-Point Game. In a single game or tie-breaker game to 21
points, the players will change ends when the first singles player
or doubles team reaches a score of 11.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: 13.G Player Contacting Net or Net Support System — Fault – Player Contacts Net or Net Support System
candidates.content:
13.G.1 Fault – Player Contacts Net or Net Support System. When a
player or anything that is worn or carried by the player contacts the
net or net support system while the ball is live, it is a fault against
the player.

candidates.heading: 25.B.3 Two-Bounce Allowance — Dead Ball
candidates.content:
25.B.3.d Dead Ball. When the ball strikes a permanent object
(e.g., fence, wall) before the second bounce, it is a
dead ball and the rally ends.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: 13.B Ball Contacting Net Support System — Fault – Ball Contacts Net Support System
candidates.content:
13.B.1 Fault – Ball Contacts Net Support System. When a player serves a
ball that contacts the net support system on either end of the net
or returns a ball that contacts the net support system before going
over the net, it is a fault against the player.

suppliedEvidence.heading: Damaged Ball
suppliedEvidence.content:
10.G Damaged Ball. When a ball is or becomes broken, cracked, soft or degraded,
play must continue until the end of the rally. The ball will be replaced if all
players agree.

suppliedEvidence.heading: 17.D Officiating Play — Damaged Balls
suppliedEvidence.content:
17.D.14 Damaged Balls. Determine whether a ball is broken or cracked
and must be replaced, and whether the broken or cracked ball
affected the outcome of a rally. (See Rule 20.F.)

suppliedEvidence.heading: 20.F Damaged Ball — Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball
suppliedEvidence.content:
20.F.1 Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball. When the referee determines
that the broken or cracked ball affected the outcome of the rally,
the rally must be replayed with a replacement ball. (Modifies
Rule 10.G.1)

suppliedEvidence.heading: Damaged Ball
suppliedEvidence.content:
20.F Damaged Ball. A player may appeal to the referee to determine whether a
ball is degraded, soft, broken, or cracked. A potentially soft or degraded
ball will not be replaced unless all players agree. If the referee determines
that the ball is broken or cracked, it will be replaced. (Modifies Rule 10.G)

suppliedEvidence.heading: 10.G Damaged Ball — Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball
suppliedEvidence.content:
10.G.1 Replay – Broken or Cracked Ball. When all players agree that a
broken or cracked ball affected the outcome of the rally, the rally
must be replayed. If all players do not agree that a broken or
cracked ball affected the outcome of the rally, the result of the rally
stands.

suppliedEvidence.heading: 10.C Returned Ball Placement — Fault – Ball Hits Player
suppliedEvidence.content:
10.C.3 Fault – Ball Hits Player. After the serve, when the ball contacts a
player or anything that is worn or carried by the player, except the
player’s paddle or the player’s hands below the wrist joint while in
contact with the paddle, it is a fault against that player.

suppliedEvidence.heading: 10.C Returned Ball Placement — Fault – Ball Hits Permanent Object After Landing
suppliedEvidence.content:
10.C.5 Fault – Ball Hits Permanent Object After Landing. When a player
fails to return a ball that has bounced in the player’s court before
the ball contacts a permanent object, it is a fault against that
player.

suppliedEvidence.heading: 25.B.3 Two-Bounce Allowance — Fault – Failure to Return Ball Before Third Bounce.
suppliedEvidence.content:
25.B.3.c Fault – Failure to Return Ball Before Third Bounce.
When the player does not return a ball before it
bounces three times, it is a fault against the player.
(Modifies Rule 10.B.1.)

authorityReviewCandidates.heading: 25.B.3 Two-Bounce Allowance — Fault – Failure to Return Ball Before Third Bounce.

bounces three times, it is a fault against the player.

authorityReviewCandidates.sectionLabel: Section 9: Dead Balls, Faults, and Hinders
authorityReviewCandidates.heading: 9.B Faults — Fault Occurrence
authorityReviewCandidates.content:
9.B.1 Fault Occurrence. A fault only occurs while the ball is live, except
for non-volley zone violations involving momentum. (See Rule
11.A.2.)

authorityReviewCandidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
authorityReviewCandidates.heading: 13.I.2 Ball Crosses Back to Opponent’s Side — Fault – Ball Not Contacted
authorityReviewCandidates.content:
13.I.2.b Fault – Ball Not Contacted. When a ball bounces in
the court on the receiving player’s end of the net and
then returns to the opponent’s end of the net without
being hit, it is a fault against a player who fails to hit
the ball before it bounces once on the opponent’s end
of the net.

authorityReviewCandidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
authorityReviewCandidates.heading: 13.E Ball Under Net — Fault – Ball Under Net
authorityReviewCandidates.content:
13.E.1 Fault – Ball Under Net. When a player hits the ball under the net, it
is a fault against the player.

authorityReviewCandidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
authorityReviewCandidates.heading: Ball Around Net Post
authorityReviewCandidates.content:
13.C Ball Around Net Post. A ball may be returned around the outside of the net
post.
