intentEvidenceCandidates.heading: LEAGUE FEES AND WAIVER
intentEvidenceCandidates.content:
LEAGUE FEES AND WAIVER
o The registration fee is per team, per division, per season, as announced before the season
begins. No refunds will be issued starting one week before the season starts, unless a division
is canceled due to having fewer than the four-team minimum or other league-initiated
cancelations.
o The League shall provide:
 Match Balls: Franklin Outdoor X-40 Optic balls for all regular season and playoƯ
matches.
 DUPR Uploads: All match results logged to DUPR for rating updates (excluding mixed
and individual Picklebreaker™ games and some tournament games).
 Administration: All scheduling, website management, and administrative support.
 Championship Prize: Free entry into the following season for the Gold Medal/1st place
team in each division based on Championship Day/PlayoƯ results.
o Waiver: As an LWR PC member, you acknowledge the risks of participation and release
LWR PC, match sites, communities/clubs, and all officers/volunteers from any claims,
liability, and costs. See the full detailed Waiver here: https://tinyurl.com/LWRPC-ClubWaiver

candidates.heading: 10.G Damaged Ball — No Replay – Soft or Degraded Ball
candidates.content:
10.G.2 No Replay – Soft or Degraded Ball. When a ball is or becomes
degraded or soft, the result of the prior rally stands.

candidates.heading: 5.C Questions About Correct Server, Receiver, and Positions — Player or Position Error Identified After Rally
candidates.content:
5.C.2 Player or Position Error Identified After Rally. When the correct
server or correct receiver is not in their correct position when the
score is called and the rally is completed, the result of the rally
stands.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: 13.B Ball Contacting Net Support System — Replay – Ball Affected by Net Support System
candidates.content:
13.B.2 Replay – Ball Affected by Net Support System. When a returned
ball crosses the net and contacts any part of a crossbar, or any
other part of the net support system within the court boundaries,
before or after the ball bounces, the rally must be replayed.

candidates.heading: Injury
candidates.content:
10.H Injury. If a player is injured during a rally, play must continue until the end of
the rally.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
candidates.heading: 13.A Ball Contacting Net — Replay – Ball Contacts Net
candidates.content:
13.A.1 Replay – Ball Contacts Net. When a returned ball that crosses the
net gets caught in the net, contacts a part of the net that is draping
on the ground, or contacts a deflecting net before or after
bouncing, the rally must be replayed.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 6: Player Readiness and Calling the
candidates.heading: 6.F Challenging the Score Call — Incorrect Score Identified After Rally
candidates.content:
6.F.4 Incorrect Score Identified After Rally. When an incorrect score
was called and the rally is completed, the result of the rally stands,
and the score must be corrected before the next serve.

candidates.heading: 25.B.3 Two-Bounce Allowance — Dead Ball
candidates.content:
25.B.3.d Dead Ball. When the ball strikes a permanent object
(e.g., fence, wall) before the second bounce, it is a
dead ball and the rally ends.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 9: Dead Balls, Faults, and Hinders
candidates.heading: 9.B.3 Calling Non-Volley Zone Faults and Service Foot Faults on — Disagreement Between Teams
candidates.content:
9.B.3.b Disagreement Between Teams. When there is any
disagreement between teams about a fault call, the rally
must be replayed.

candidates.heading: 5.C.1 Player or Position Error Claimed During Rally — Replay – Correct Claim
candidates.content:
5.C.1.a Replay – Correct Claim. If the correct server or correct
receiver is not in their correct position when the score
is called and a player stops the rally to correctly
identify the player or position error, the rally must be
replayed.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 6: Player Readiness and Calling the
candidates.heading: 6.F Challenging the Score Call — Replay – Incorrect Score Called
candidates.content:
6.F.1 Replay – Incorrect Score Called. When an incorrect score is called
and the rally is stopped before the return of serve and before the
ball becomes dead, the rally must be replayed with the correct
score called.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 6: Player Readiness and Calling the
candidates.heading: Challenging the Score Call
candidates.content:
6.F Challenging the Score Call. A player may stop a rally to ask for a score
correction before the return of serve is hit and before the ball becomes dead.

candidates.heading: Player Equipment or Apparel Problem
candidates.content:
10.I Player Equipment or Apparel Problem. If a player experiences an
equipment or apparel problem during a rally, play must continue until the
end of the rally.

candidates.heading: 25.B.2 Assistive Devices — Prohibited Use
candidates.content:
25.B.2.b Prohibited Use. Assistive devices must not be used
to strike the ball or to intentionally alter its flight. If
an assistive device contacts a live ball, the ball
becomes dead and the rally ends.

candidates.heading: 22.A Referee Authorization — Timing of Assessment
candidates.content:
22.A.1 Timing of Assessment. Play will not be stopped to assess a
warning or foul. The assessment will be applied after the rally
has ended.

candidates.heading: Replay – Server or Position Correction
candidates.content:
20.C Replay – Server or Position Correction. When the referee stops a rally to
identify a player or position error, the rally must be replayed.

candidates.heading: 7.B.3 Visible Release — Replay – Ball Release Not Visible
candidates.content:
7.B.3.a Replay – Ball Release Not Visible. When the receiver
cannot see the release of the ball, the receiver may call
for a replay, but only before the return of serve.

candidates.heading: Extra Ball
candidates.content:
24.B Extra Ball. An extra ball carried by a player during a rally must not be
visible to the opponent and must remain in possession of the player.

candidates.heading: 20.E.2 Replays — Replay – Drop Serve, Questionable Force on Ball.
candidates.content:
20.E.2.i Replay – Drop Serve, Questionable Force on Ball.
When it is questionable whether the ball was
propelled when the server released the ball to make
a drop serve, the referee must call for a replay.

candidates.heading: No Definitive Call by Referee
candidates.content:
19.G No Definitive Call by Referee. When the referee is unable to make a call
upon appeal, the outcome of the rally is determined by Rules 19.G.1
through 19.G.4.

candidates.heading: 20.E.2 Replays — Replay – Questionable Manipulation or Spin
candidates.content:
20.E.2.c Replay – Questionable Manipulation or Spin. When
it is questionable whether the server imparted
manipulation or spin during the release of the ball,
the referee may call for a replay. (Modifies Rule
7.B.2.a)

candidates.heading: 10.C Returned Ball Placement — Fault – Ball Hits Permanent Object After Landing
candidates.content:
10.C.5 Fault – Ball Hits Permanent Object After Landing. When a player
fails to return a ball that has bounced in the player’s court before
the ball contacts a permanent object, it is a fault against that
player.

candidates.heading: 5.C Questions About Correct Server, Receiver, and Positions — Player or Position Error Claimed During Rally
candidates.content:
5.C.1 Player or Position Error Claimed During Rally. Any player may
stop a rally to claim an incorrect server, incorrect receiver, or
incorrect player position.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 9: Dead Balls, Faults, and Hinders
candidates.heading: 9.A Stopping a Rally — Fault – Stopping a Rally
candidates.content:
9.A.1 Fault – Stopping a Rally. When a player stops a rally before the
ball otherwise becomes dead, it is a fault against the player unless
the stoppage is to call a hinder (see Rule 9.C), to correctly identify a
player position or server error (see Rule 5.C.1.a), or to ask for
correction of an incorrect score before the return of serve (see Rule
6.F.1).

candidates.heading: Standard Scoring
candidates.content:
4.A Standard Scoring. A point is scored by serving the ball and winning the
rally. (See Rule 14.A.2 for the rally scoring option.)

candidates.heading: 7.B.2 No Manipulation or Spin Upon Release — Replay – Manipulation or Spin Added
candidates.content:
7.B.2.a Replay – Manipulation or Spin Added. When the
receiver determines that the server has imparted
manipulation or spin during the release of the ball, the
receiver may call for a replay, but only before returning
the serve.

candidates.heading: 25.B.3 Two-Bounce Allowance — Fault – Failure to Return Ball Before Third Bounce.
candidates.content:
25.B.3.c Fault – Failure to Return Ball Before Third Bounce.
When the player does not return a ball before it
bounces three times, it is a fault against the player.
(Modifies Rule 10.B.1.)

players agree.

authorityReviewCandidates.content:

the rally must be replayed with a replacement ball. (Modifies
Rule 10.G.1)

authorityReviewCandidates.heading: Damaged Ball
authorityReviewCandidates.content:
20.F Damaged Ball. A player may appeal to the referee to determine whether a

that the ball is broken or cracked, it will be replaced. (Modifies Rule 10.G)

authorityReviewCandidates.heading: 10.G Damaged Ball — No Replay – Soft or Degraded Ball
authorityReviewCandidates.content:
10.G.2 No Replay – Soft or Degraded Ball. When a ball is or becomes
degraded or soft, the result of the prior rally stands.

authorityReviewCandidates.heading: 5.C Questions About Correct Server, Receiver, and Positions — Player or Position Error Identified After Rally
authorityReviewCandidates.content:
5.C.2 Player or Position Error Identified After Rally. When the correct
server or correct receiver is not in their correct position when the
score is called and the rally is completed, the result of the rally
stands.

authorityReviewCandidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
authorityReviewCandidates.heading: 13.B Ball Contacting Net Support System — Replay – Ball Affected by Net Support System
authorityReviewCandidates.content:
13.B.2 Replay – Ball Affected by Net Support System. When a returned
ball crosses the net and contacts any part of a crossbar, or any
other part of the net support system within the court boundaries,
before or after the ball bounces, the rally must be replayed.

authorityReviewCandidates.heading: Injury
authorityReviewCandidates.content:
10.H Injury. If a player is injured during a rally, play must continue until the end of
the rally.

authorityReviewCandidates.sectionLabel: Section 13: The Net and Net Support
authorityReviewCandidates.heading: 13.A Ball Contacting Net — Replay – Ball Contacts Net
authorityReviewCandidates.content:
13.A.1 Replay – Ball Contacts Net. When a returned ball that crosses the
net gets caught in the net, contacts a part of the net that is draping
on the ground, or contacts a deflecting net before or after
bouncing, the rally must be replayed.

authorityReviewCandidates.sectionLabel: Section 6: Player Readiness and Calling the
authorityReviewCandidates.heading: 6.F Challenging the Score Call — Incorrect Score Identified After Rally
authorityReviewCandidates.content:
6.F.4 Incorrect Score Identified After Rally. When an incorrect score
was called and the rally is completed, the result of the rally stands,
and the score must be corrected before the next serve.

authorityReviewCandidates.heading: 25.B.3 Two-Bounce Allowance — Dead Ball
authorityReviewCandidates.content:
25.B.3.d Dead Ball. When the ball strikes a permanent object
(e.g., fence, wall) before the second bounce, it is a
dead ball and the rally ends.

candidates.content:
20.C Replay – Server or Position Correction. When the referee stops a rally to
identify a player or position error, the rally must be replayed.

candidates.heading: 5.C.1 Player or Position Error Claimed During Rally — Replay – Correct Claim
candidates.content:
5.C.1.a Replay – Correct Claim. If the correct server or correct
receiver is not in their correct position when the score
is called and a player stops the rally to correctly
identify the player or position error, the rally must be
replayed.

candidates.heading: 20.E.2 Replays — Replay – Questionable Release From One Hand,
candidates.content:
20.E.2.b Replay – Questionable Release From One Hand,
Paddle or Natural Height. When it is questionable
whether the server released the ball from only one
hand or only from the paddle, or whether the release
on a drop serve was from a natural (un-aided) height,
the referee may call for a replay.

candidates.heading: 19.I Player Override of Call — Replay or Concession – Player Override of Official’s “Out”
candidates.content:
19.I.1 Replay or Concession – Player Override of Official’s “Out”
Call. When a player disagrees with a line judge’s or a referee’s
“out” call that favored the player, the rally must be replayed,
unless the player concedes the rally to their opponent.

candidates.heading: 20.E.2 Replays — Replay – Volley Serve, Questionable Paddle Head
candidates.content:
20.E.2.g Replay – Volley Serve, Questionable Paddle Head
Height. When it is questionable whether the highest
point of the paddle head was no higher than the
server’s wrist joint when the paddle contacted the
ball to make a volley serve, the referee may call for a
replay.

candidates.heading: 20.E.2 Replays — Replay – Questionable Foot Contact Outside the
candidates.content:
20.E.2.e Replay – Questionable Foot Contact Outside the
Serving Area. When it is questionable whether either
of the server’s feet were in contact with the playing
surface outside the serving area when the paddle
contacted the ball, the referee may call for a replay.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 6: Player Readiness and Calling the
candidates.heading: Replay – Player Repositioning
candidates.content:
6.D.2 Replay – Player Repositioning. When the serving team changes
serving areas after the score has been called, the server must allow
all players to reposition, and then the score must be re-called to
restart the 10-second count.

candidates.heading: 20.E.2 Replays — Replay – Drop Serve, Questionable Force on Ball.
candidates.content:
20.E.2.i Replay – Drop Serve, Questionable Force on Ball.
When it is questionable whether the ball was
propelled when the server released the ball to make
a drop serve, the referee must call for a replay.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 9: Dead Balls, Faults, and Hinders
candidates.heading: 9.C Hinders — Replay – Hinder
candidates.content:
9.C.2 Replay – Hinder. When a hinder is called, the rally must be
replayed.

candidates.heading: 20.E.2 Replays — Replay – Questionable Foot Contact with Serving
candidates.content:
20.E.2.d Replay – Questionable Foot Contact with Serving
Area. When it is questionable whether either of the
server’s feet were in contact with the serving area
when the paddle contacted the ball, the referee may
call for a replay.

candidates.heading: 19.G No Definitive Call by Referee — Replay – No Call by Officiating Team
candidates.content:
19.G.4 Replay – No Call by Officiating Team. When the line judges and
referees are unable to make a call, the rally must be replayed.

candidates.heading: 21.B End Change Time-Out — Resuming Play
candidates.content:
21.B.8 Resuming Play. The referee will resume play by announcing a
15-second warning (Rule 17.D.16).

candidates.heading: 21.D Referee Time-Out — Resuming Play
candidates.content:

15-second warning (Rule 17.D.16).

candidates.content:

candidates.heading: 21.A Standard Time-Out — Resuming Play
candidates.content:

candidates.heading: 20.E.2 Replays — Replay – Volley Serve, Questionable Ball Height.
candidates.content:
20.E.2.h Replay – Volley Serve, Questionable Ball Height.
When it is questionable whether the ball was no
higher than the server’s waist when the paddle
contacted the ball to make a volley serve, the referee
may call for a replay.

candidates.sectionLabel: Section 9: Dead Balls, Faults, and Hinders
candidates.heading: 9.B.3 Calling Non-Volley Zone Faults and Service Foot Faults on — Disagreement Between Teams
candidates.content:
9.B.3.b Disagreement Between Teams. When there is any
disagreement between teams about a fault call, the rally
must be replayed.

candidates.heading: 25.A.12 Tournament Events — Replay – Questionable Wheel Contact Outside
candidates.content:
25.A.12.c Replay – Questionable Wheel Contact Outside
the Serving Area. When it is questionable whether
a large rear wheel of the server’s wheelchair was in
contact with the playing surface outside the
serving area when the serve was hit, the referee
may call for a replay. (Modifies Rule 20.E.2.e)

candidates.heading: 19.F Referee Overrule of Line Call — Replay or Concession – Referee Overrule of Line Judge’s
candidates.content:
19.F.2 Replay or Concession – Referee Overrule of Line Judge’s
“Out” Call. When the referee overrules a line judge’s “out” call
as “in,” the rally must be replayed, unless the singles player or
doubles team that benefits from the referee’s ruling concedes
the rally to their opponent.

candidates.heading: 21.E Equipment Time-Out — Resuming Play
candidates.content:
21.E.2 Resuming Play. The referee will resume play by announcing a
15-second warning (Rule 17.D.16).
